items.body:
There is a moment on "Tea Horse Road," the album's fourth track, where the saxophone drops to a near whisper and the percussion seems to breathe rather than strike. You realize you are not listening to two musicians from opposite sides of the world so much as two people who have agreed, without a word, on exactly how much silence costs.

Lao Dan grew up in Northeastern China near the North Korean border. He showed enough early talent on saxophone and bamboo flute to earn a place at conservatory, then walked away from it. He studied dizi formally in Beijing and later at Shenyang Conservatory before turning toward avant-garde jazz and free improvisation around 2013. What he took from that training was not obedience. It was control: a deep physical understanding of breath through a tube, and an instinct for space that most Western free players spend decades trying to locate.

Barcelona-based Vasco Trilla came to the drums late, at nineteen, through progressive rock and metal. He worked his way outward through jazz, African music, and free improvisation. He has since appeared on more than a hundred recordings for labels including NoBusiness, Clean Feed, and Cuneiform. He plays like a man who understands that the wrong note at the right moment is still the wrong note.

The seven tracks here, from the opener "You Are You" through the closing "Nobodies Are Going to Sleep," feel less like a set list than a field journal. Lao Dan moves between tenor saxophone and dizi (Chinese flute), changing not just tone but altitude. Trilla generates rhythm without always generating a pulse, which is a different and harder skill. On "Fire Boy," Dan's flute cuts upward in tight spirals while Trilla accelerates with the controlled intensity of someone who knows exactly how hot to let things get. "Tea Horse Road," named for the ancient trade route connecting Yunnan to Tibet, sits at the emotional center. It is patient, unresolved, and genuinely rooted. The drummer shakes what sounds like a string of small cymbals while giving Dan a wide, open background. As the piece heats up, the intensity feels both grounded and spiritually convincing.

The closing track thins out slowly until you are not sure whether you are still listening or simply sitting in the room where the music happened. It is a good place to leave things.

You Are You; New Species 1; New Species 2; Tea Horse Road; Old Heaven Books; Fire Boy; Nobodies Are Going to Sleep.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是中国吹管乐手老丹与巴塞罗那鼓手Vasco Trilla的自由即兴二重奏录音。老丹在次中音萨克斯与竹笛之间切换，将中国东北地区的传统气息注入前卫即兴语境；Trilla以丰富的自由演奏经验，在打击节奏与无声之间构建精密的张力。七首作品以茶马古道为意象核心，呈现跨文化对话中克制与爆发的平衡。专辑由知名独立小厂牌发行，定位为深度自由即兴的实验录音，在东方管乐与欧洲前卫鼓击的交汇处探索声音的空间感与呼吸感。

items.body:
On his first solo album, Paris-based Iranian artist Cinna Peyghamy (who's worked alongside Saint Abdullah & Eomac, David August, Azu Tiwaline and O.M. Theorem) plugs into a Persia that exists in only his heart by moving far beyond its boundaries, playing impossible tombak and setar sequences and disrupting them with uncanny modular processes.

Peyghamy has been working on 'Music for Tombak and Synth' since 2019, when his master's thesis research into contact microphones led him to consider sound design as a way to explore his Persian roots. He'd been working as a producer and a performer in parallel for years but has rarely unified his various approaches on record: 'Music for Tombak & Synth' gave him the opportunity to expand on the "performance-ready setup" he'd been working on with tombak and a modular system for the last few years and simultaneously examine his cultural heritage, the Iran he'd experienced via his family despite being an exile. He sees each of the album's eight compositions as deeply personal "keepsakes" that anchor the material in lived experiences, but it also never sounds nostalgic. Far from it, in fact; Peyghamy's layered rhythms and glassy synths are jarringly futuristic, sounding closer to Mohammad Reza Mortazavi's elasticated experiments, or even Sote's modernist folk reboot 'Parallel Persia'.

He's loath to describe the material as "electroacoustic" and we can hear why. The rhythms and indeed some of the melodic elements are undoubtedly rooted in acoustic instruments, but Peyghamy pulls the sounds up by their stalks, re-planting them in unfamiliar soil. And the process, while roughly the same for each composition, often yields very different results. Opener 'Mutosy' materializes in a dubwise space, coating its tombak rhythms in comb-filtered, ping-ponging reverberations that wouldn't sound out of place on a Monolake record and adding plodding bass that seems to work against the high-end rhythms, creating an unsettling clockwork effect. 'Zur زور' meanwhile sounds ritualistic in comparison, meeting its stirring rhythms in a wide open outdoor space, with metallic, xenharmonic melodies sounding like alien flutes or mechanical bird calls in the distance. Setar twangs slow dance with stuttering modular belches on the brilliant 'La Nesque', creating another dimension for Peyghamy to explore, and on the album's thematic centerpiece 'Dar Shab در شب', the artist's dad (who also took the album's evocative cover photo) appears, reciting a poem from iconic Iranian poet, writer and journalist Ahmad Shamlou over Peyghamy jr's reverberant soundscape. Another winner for Nicolas Jaar's Other People imprint.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑将波斯传统乐器通巴克鼓和塞塔尔琴与模块化合成器进行深度融合，以极具实验性的声音设计探索流散者对故土的文化记忆。八首作品根植于波斯音乐语汇，却呈现出强烈的未来感，节奏层次丰富，音色在声学与电子之间不断转化。专辑拒绝怀旧叙事，以拼贴式的合成纹理和异律旋律构建出独特的声响空间，兼具个人抒情与前卫实验气质。作为居巴黎的伊朗裔艺术家的首张个人专辑，其跨文化身份为创作提供了独到的视角，Nicolas Jaar旗下独立厂牌Other People的发行定位也精准契合此类跨领域实验作品。

items.body:
The craziest label in Detroit back with another genius, unfathomable dose of destroyed Techno x Trip Metal, caked in Motor City crud and located on the factory line somewhere between Urban Tribe, H-Fusion and Wolf Eyes​

Seven years on from his debut ‘Bloodsport’, secretive 313 artist K-6000 only jags deeper into Detroit’s scuzzy underbelly on the rough hewn rhythmic noise and atmospheric trip metal of ‘War Games’. The 6-part album surely evokes the dystopia of modern Detroit’s knackered architecture in its cranky tone and offbeat structure, but also signals the underlying soul of its entities, and the lost futures they live thru, in its textured play of psyched sax and guitar spectres meshed with sampledelic tapestry of disembodied voices. 

A record that leaves dirt under yr nails, it unfurls at its own steady pace from free jazz noise like some Wolf Eyes re-score of Robocop, into grouchy bouts of squashed beatdown psych with ruggedest drum programming comparable to KDJ, Shake and Sherard Ingram’s chops with Kemetrix on the Urban Tribe album. It descends into the sleaziest mire of Blind Pig biker bar blooz, like Captain Beefheart jamming with H-Fusion, around the mid-section, and ultimately buckles into PCP-spiked industrial funk sludge in the final stages. 

Manna for sci-fi free jazz trip metal beatdown hounds, then!
items._cn_summary: 底特律地下艺术家K-6000的专辑《War Games》将破坏性Techno、节奏噪音与自由即兴爵士熔于一炉，融入迷幻萨克斯、残响吉他与碎片化人声采样，呈现出浓郁的工业废墟质感。整张作品横跨Trip Metal、Free Jazz Noise、工业放克污泥等多个领域，结构自由松散，音色粗粝黑暗，带有强烈的后工业城市美学气息。评论将其与Wolf Eyes、Urban Tribe、Captain Beefheart等实验先驱并列，突出其在底特律地下场景中独特的声音实验路径，是面向极端实验听众的地下制作。

items.body:
The precocious, recombinant jazz talents of a 22 year old Michael Gregory Jackson, and pals, are beautifully captured on his 1977 debut, yielding early shoots of his pop ambitions in Jacquardian weaves of jazz-fusion, neo-classical and flamenco, with unique appeal.

Stemming from mid ‘70s free jazz roots with empathic players, Oliver Lake, David Murray & Wadada Leo Smith, a young Jackson beautifully took the lead on debut album ‘Clarity’ with a mix of advanced musicality and naïf wanderlust yielding singular results. Shifting with a striking elegance beyond his years, from free jazz to ballads, flamenco and sinuous, angular neoclassical minimalism, the album remains a strangely calming yet quizzical curio in its field, yet wholly characteristic of developments in jazz at the time. 50 years after the fact, it’s hard not to be enamoured with its ambitious scope and reserved discipline.

The titular opening gambit is a total gem, initially smudging distinctions of jazz and chamber classical, before a gorgeous R&B soul vocal lands from above, and you just know it’s going to get special. Funnily enough, that voice doesn’t appear again for the rest of the album, but that quite alright as the instrumentalists pucker and stretch out with a mix of vividly lyrical and conversational qualities, even in a ‘Ballad’ whose title would surely imply a voice in there somewhere. From a pastoral gem ‘A View of This Life’ recalling aspects of Luciano Cilio, thru quietly breathtaking take on classical flamenco in ‘Prelueoionti’ foreshadowing Jim O’Rourke tekkerz, to almost Stockhausen-esque angularity in ‘CLARITY 4’, and its sublime closer ‘IOMI’, it’s deeply impressive stuff.

TIP!
items._cn_summary: 1977年，年仅22岁的Michael Gregory Jackson首张专辑，与自由爵士名家Oliver Lake、David Murray、Wadada Leo Smith合作。专辑根植于七十年代中期自由爵士脉络，融合新古典极简主义、弗拉门戈与爵士融合元素，展现出超越年龄的成熟与野心。曲风从自由即兴到抒情民谣、弗拉门戈、棱角分明的古典极简主义之间自由转换，呈现出静谧而引人好奇的独特气质。评论将其与Luciano Cilio、Jim O'Rourke、Stockhausen等艺术家风格相联系，体现出宽广的美学谱系。整体为融合多重前卫元素的自由爵士跨界佳作，兼具学术深度与年轻创作者的探索活力。

items.body:
Copenhagen’s meme-able, custom line of genre-blurring songwriters yields Lithuanian talent, Gintè Preisait, fresh from the conservatoire and an LP with Toshimaru Nakamura, on an enchanted, waking dream blend of lower case concrète, trip hop and avant-classical experimentation calling to mind the refined crafts of ML Buch, Ugné Uma, Svitlana Nianio, Smerz, Lucrecia Dalt, Julia Holter or Martyna Basta, thru the reaches of Finland’s Fonal Records.

It was bound to happen at some point, right? We've written more than enough about how Copenhagen's Rhythmic Music Conservatory has become the central node in a scene that's prioritized the permeable membrane between pop, classical training and unhinged technological experimentation - honestly where else are you gonna find Clarissa Connelly, Astrid Sonne, Erika de Casier, ML Buch and Fine? Gintė Preisaitė pushes even further into uncharted waters on her debut album, letting the pop forms evaporate like vapors around her intricately woven experimental collages. We're already off to a good start with 'Vigilance', a lengthy introduction that pays its respects to Preisaitė's past, present and future. The classically trained improviser, producer and composer begins with an ensemble of moaning acoustic instruments that she gradually chips into, tearing through the acoustic sounds with electronic treatments and introducing subtle, grounding field recordings before adding her voice and completely shifting the direction. 

The unwieldy blend of elements prepares us for an arguably bolder experiment, 'Summary Saint Mary', where Preisaitė matches her gamelan-like prepared piano phrases with Björk-ish vocal loops, OPN-inspired electronic touches and wheezing processed acoustic sounds. And it's remarkably well controlled; even in capable hands, it's a tough palette to work with and Preisaitė makes it look almost easy, never stepping too far in any direction or another. Because it's not really a pop record at all, it's an album that's aware of pop, doesn't avoid its charms, but manages to corral its characteristics into the avant garde's misshapen spirit. Even the relatively upbeat, straightforward 'Aéroport', a track that would have sounded stylistically comfortable on Smerz's RMC love-in 'Big city life EDITS', she never goes full James K, letting the melodies curve towards freeform abstraction in the final act before hitting us with three tracks of choppy, half-dissolved prepared piano. It's ambitious stuff, and all the better for it.
items._cn_summary: 立陶宛音乐人Gintė Preisaitė的首张专辑，融合了小写具体音乐、trip hop与前卫古典实验，编织出层次繁复的声音拼贴。作品以预制钢琴为核心，叠加电子处理、田野录音与人声循环，在具象与抽象之间游走。Preisaitė毕业于哥本哈根节奏音乐学院，深受该校跨界实验氛围影响，她的创作既不回避流行元素的形式感，又将其收编进前卫精神的框架内。专辑展现出扎实的古典训练背景与对实验声响的敏锐直觉，控制力出色，风格在Lucrecia Dalt、Julia Holter等人的参照系中找到了自己的位置。作为东欧艺术家的独立厂牌作品，兼具地域文化视角与跨国实验语境的独特融合。

items.body: Hannah Peel & Beibei Wang The Endless Dance Arpeggiating electronics meet Chinese water percussion, temple bells and rice bowls on an album that ends up sounding far more coherent and harmonious than it has any right to The Endless Dance by Hannah Peel Traditional Chinese percussion and contemporary polyrhythmic electronica – it’s a pairing that should feel like using an iPhone to light a fire. But by the end of Hannah Peel and Beibei Wang’s collaborative album, The Endless Dance, you might find yourself asking, why has nobody thought of this before? The short answer would be that there aren’t many artists out there who could synthesise Peel and Wang’s varied but equally impressive resumés. Both artists share classical backgrounds, with Wang well-versed in both... The post Hannah Peel & Beibei Wang – The Endless Dance appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张融合中国传统打击乐（水锣、寺庙铜铃、米碗等）与当代电子音乐的跨界合作专辑，由英国电子音乐人Hannah Peel与中国演奏家Beibei Wang共同完成。两位艺术家均具备古典音乐背景，却选择了看似不太可能的组合方向——传统中国节奏体系与多层次电子声响的碰撞。专辑被评价为比预期更加统一和谐，琶音电子音色与中国水打击乐形成有机对话，体现了跨文化音乐融合的实验性探索。该作品在世界音乐、电子实验及当代古典之间找到了交汇点，对偏爱跨界融合与声音实验的听众具有较强吸引力。原文内容因截断而信息不完整，但已传递出核心音乐概念与风格定位。

items.body: Grief comes in multiple shapes and forms. None of them are pleasing to the eye or the ear. On 2:25, Alessandro Brivio confronts loss as a system under stress, short-circuiting in real time. The cover image—a specular photograph of graffiti spelling La Morte Non Ha Senso (Death Makes No Sense), doubled and inverted into near illegibility—sets the tone for a record that refuses clarity, mirroring the cognitive disarray of loss. Since his debut 6pezzi2009+lagodelnulla on Senufo, Brivio has explored loops and rhythmic repetition, often drawing from African patterns; here, those tendencies collapse inward, mutating into jammed circuits and malfunctioning systems. The opening track, “Cerchi” (26’03”), could stand alone as a release: an abrasive, confrontational expanse where different systems collide, forced through extreme processing and splintering into stuttering, unstable configurations. There are moments when the tension subsides, although the underlying rage keeps the momentum going. What once felt like carefully balanced studies now teeters on the edge of rupture, as if the material itself were resisting containment, at the risk of wearing itself out. Across the remaining tracks, Brivio sketches a fractured cartography of grief’s non-linear stages—denial, anger, bargaining, depression, acceptance—without ever settling into them. “Diarismi” and “3.03” continue the tension between separation and collapse, their stratified layers suggesting a kind of sonic bargaining, each element vying for space yet never fully coalescing. It is midway through “Controra” that a fragile shift occurs: the density thins, and a subdued, almost hollowed atmosphere emerges, hinting at acceptance without fully embracing it. These quieter passages feel like depression folding back into reflection. The album closes with “VV,” a 21-second drift that exhales with no catharsis, no closure—only the faint release of pressure. Composed during a difficult period in 2025 as a tribute to a lost friend, 2:25 stands as a work of raw processing, where sound itself becomes both the site and the residue of mourning, revealing the process in all its necessary and inevitable messiness. (Gianmarco Del Re)
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以实验电子为核心语汇，融合世界音乐节奏脉络与工业噪音质感。Alessandro Brivio 以极端声音处理、短路化的循环结构以及二十六分钟级的长篇铺陈，将哀悼主题转化为系统崩溃般的声响景观。失序的拼贴美学贯穿全作：信号阻塞、分层剥落、动态断裂，与封套上'死亡毫无意义'的镜像涂鸦形成互文。Senufo 厂牌的发行背景印证了其地下实验属性，长篇作品中张力的积聚与压强的间歇释放构成核心聆听体验，是面向先锋听众的原始声响处理之作。

items.body:
More gorgeous, hazed dreamweaving from mysterio label wherethetimegoes - the same crew that gave us a pair of stunners from Princ€ss and Nashpaints, here dissolving Dublin's special blend of peak Celtic futurism into a suite of effervescent fiddle-laced electroacoustic experiments that turn everyday musical elements into vivid, lysergic space-age landscapes, smeared with VHS infidelities.

Like Princ€ss, we've no idea who Dublin are - they're a "post modern classical" duo, as far as we can tell - but there's at least a breadcrumb trail. They emerged back in 2022 on wherethetimegoes with a CDr of bizarre jams, seemingly on violin and synth, that put them fully into their own zone, seamlessly blending Celtic folk music, West Coast new age, Eno-esque ambient and downtown-era improv without even trying to flex. 'Heavy Dublin' picks up where that set left off, presenting a similarly anonymous sequence of jams that pack into roughly the same creative space. "Oh," a voice exclaims in the opening seconds of 'Untitled 4', heralding a thick wall of digital synths and soundscapes that's sliced thru by a Conrad-esque pitch-wonked violin performance that's amplified in a way that's at odds with the other sounds. It's almost drawing a line in the sand, exclaiming that the fiddle is from our world and doesn't need to be sculpted to fit into another. And it's the perfect introduction.

On 'Untitled 2', the vibrating, powdery fiddle improvisations shiver across the kind of rhythmic, metallophone-like synth loops that you might find on any number of early Detroit techno b-sides. It's a canny reference, using two distinct future projections to create something new, an off-world cogitation from an unmistakably contemporary source that projects past the stratosphere towards a 'Solaris'-style space station. And the atmosphere continues to grow on 'Untitled 3', with subtlly glitchy rhythmic interjections that interrupt the flow of brushed aluminum synths and mangled acoustic instrumentation. It's Visible Cloaks' Fairlight futures meets Laura Cannell's archeofiction, a muddle of imaginations that pull us backwards and forwards on the timeline all at once. Similarly, there's a trace of Arthur Russell's reverb-heavy 'World of Echo' steez on 'Untitled 7', caught in a tangle of bit-chewed samples and noisy digital outbursts.

The album seems to build up to 'Untitled 5', a weightless cloud of steel pan loops, obscured voices, chimes and harmonically rich fiddle scrapes that sounds as if it's hanging off the timeline by a thread, linking Takehisa Kosugi's 'Catch Wave' concept into a catalog of sounds that you'd more readily find in the world of tape traders and private press 12"s. Fully mind-melting gear, no doubt.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由神秘二人组Dublin创作，在独立小厂牌wherethetimegoes发行，以小提琴与合成器为核心乐器。作品将凯尔特民间音乐、西海岸新世纪氛围、Eno式环境音乐以及纽约下城即兴传统融为一体，形成电声实验框架。编曲手法上，数字合成器质感与原声提琴形成鲜明对比，电子节奏结构借鉴早期底特律铁克诺，辅以磁带循环、位元失真人声采样等手法。整体游离于当代古典、实验电子与世界音乐之间，呈现出空灵、迷幻的太空感与离地氛围，定位明确指向先锋听觉审美。

items.body:
If Devon Rexi did Memphis-meets-chaabi-and-singeli, it may sound like Nicolini’s latest for their shared label South of North, melding fanciful, Arabic-style autotune and fizzing offbeats with trunk-rattle 808s in rudest, loosey-goosey style.

‘Quita Maldicion’ is Nicola Reverda’s 6th solo release on the label since his 2021 debut, over which time both artist and label have become go-to’s for weirdo, outernational-flavoured bops. The album’s 11 succinct vignettes tile up to a type of crazy-paving space between styles, Magpieing aspects of Memphis rap and Mahraganat dance-pop with a dub-wise, post-punk license and cheeky funk that works a treat, just like his chops with Devon Rexi - arguably one of the hottest live bands on road right now, especially with John T. Gast on the mixing desk. 

It’s not hard to hear Nicolini’s input on Devon Rexi surface across the album, from its spicy sirens and animated idents to the deftness of his wrong-footing grooves. It’s all there in centrepiece ‘Bottle J’, where steppas bass collides hip-shot sampler stabs and autotune, and likewise in ‘Girma Come In My Light’, but zipped up on a deep south rap downstroke. He’s also prone to hybridise gothic rap bells with grimy soca drums on ‘Rompe Mi Cabeza’, and fuse singeli with flamenco on ‘BBY Spoon’, or go like haywire digickal steppas on ‘Deep Tissue Killa Riddim’, all primed to send a dance hectic.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是音乐人Nicolini（真名Nicola Reverda）在独立小厂牌South of North发行的第六张个人作品。音乐将孟菲斯说唱、埃及Mahraganat电子舞曲、坦桑尼亚singeli、北非chaabi、加勒比soca、弗拉门戈、dub与后朋克等多种风格拼贴融合。制作上采用阿拉伯式autotune处理、808低音和碎裂的切分节奏，11首短小曲目拼合成跨风格的马赛克空间。混音由John T. Gast操刀。整张专辑定位为怪趣的国际化俱乐部热单，强调跨文化碰撞与舞蹈功能性，属于小众全球低音场景中的混血实验产物。

items.body:
New LP from Italo-Vietnamese Brussels-based artist Radio Hito via Meakusma & Bologna label Maple Death - "a ten-sequence song cycle for voice and MIDI soundfonts adapted from the 2021 book by French poet Claude Royet-Journoud"

"Certain paths necessitate and call for one singular long sequence in order to arrive at a fully formed conversation or reasoning. Nothing seems to broadcast it more clearly than the trajectory Brussels based Italo-Vietnamese artist Nguyễn Zen Mỹ embarked on during the last decade as Radio Hito.

After a string of highly cherished and sought out tape releases, Radio Hito’s new album ‘L’uso e gli attributi del cuore’, co-released by Maple Death & Meakusma, unfolds with devastating clarity, a profound balance of depth, minimalism and emotional grounding. A ten-sequence song cycle for voice and MIDI soundfonts adapted from the 2021 book by French poet Claude Royet-Journoud.

Written and recorded between January 2023 and August 2025, the cycle evolved through nearly 80 live performances from Galicia to Kazakhstan before arriving at its recorded form. Set to an Italian libretto adapted from Royet-Journoud’s text ‘L'usage et les attributs du cœur’ (POL, 2021), the work revisits the tradition of the 19th-century Lied — art song built on existing poetry— transposed into a radically economical contemporary setting: voice and Casio CTK workstations.

"I was interested by this incompleteness CRJ mentions - by the ‘suspension’ of meaning questioning readability and intelligibility. I ‘resisted’ to CRJ’s texts since I met him and got to know his work. […] It seems to me that when playing the songs, I submit an object to be completed by the audience."

Radio Hito’s distinctive approach to setting poetry to music — spare arrangements, strophic repetition, and a voice suspended between recital, fm transmission and canzone — creates a language of its own, reaching new heights on ‘L’uso e gli attributi del cuore’, songs that are formally rigorous, emotionally restrained, and shaped by the discipline of sustained live performance, interlocking into a coherent cycle.

Rather than illustrating the poem, Radio Hito approaches it as a space of suspension. Royet-Journoud described poetry as a “profession of ignorance” where meaning remains incomplete; these songs extend that trembling state, allowing repetition, digital timbre, and restraint to hold the text open.

Often misread as minimal synth or romantic chanson, Radio Hito’s practice is rooted instead in the lineage of the art song and song cycle: open structures, close attention to language, and a live performance economy that pushes the voice at the heart of the stage. The choice of accessible keyboard workstations — light, portable, and embedded in contemporary popular culture — replaces the historical piano.

Radio Hito creates fantastical, mirage-like songs, intimate yet elusive. Her music is forlorn chanson for the digital age; bringing her haunting and beautiful vocalisations into conversation with MIDI soundfonts and humble-yet-deep casio compositions. Music that strides for simplicity, yet lands miraculously within an entire new universe, a uniqueness achieved from like-minded spirits such as Ghedalia Tazartès, Savina Yannatou & Lena Platonos, Dorothy Carter, cycles that trickle down into estuaries."
items._cn_summary: Radio Hito（Nguyễn Zen Mỹ）是一位常驻布鲁塞尔的意越混血艺术家，这张专辑是与Meakusma和Maple Death两个独立厂牌合作发行的十乐章声乐套曲。作品改编自法国诗人Claude Royet-Journoud的2021年诗作，以意大利文歌词呈现，人声搭配Casio CTK键盘的MIDI音色，将十九世纪艺术歌曲（Lied）传统转译为极简的当代数字语境。专辑经过近八十场现场演出打磨而成，以稀疏的编配、反复的分节结构以及悬浮于朗诵、FM广播与意大利民歌之间的嗓音质感，构建出独特的声学空间。整体定位介于当代古典、实验人声艺术与低保真电子之间，呈现出亲密而难以捉听的数字时代香颂气质。

items.body:
Following up 2024's Fibonacci-friendly 'Yucca', producer Church Andrews and percussionist Matt Davies return with an ear-bending set of skewed xenharmonic thizzlers that'll hit the spot if yr into Rian Treanor, Aleksi Perälä, Eli Keszler or Squarepusher.

Andrews and Davies know their shit, that's for sure. If you can level any criticism at them, it's that they know too much, in fact. Initially inspired by Terry Riley, John Coltrane and Dilla, they developed their style by jamming with a keyboard and drum kid, mimicking DAW-brained IDM and fractal generated biz until they reached the level of Japanese titans goat (JP), where you can hardly tell whether you're listening to a group of humans or a Max/MSP patch loaded up with algorithms. They continue to challenge themselves on 'Tilt', complicating the rhythms even further and introducing the kind of chiming microtonalities you'd expect to hear on any number of Perälä's thousands of releases. 

On 'Sheperd', it's a little disconcerting at first, like hearing a Tom Jenkinson 12" that's stuck on a wonky turntable. But loosen yr mind into the groove and everything begins to make sense; after the clockwork funk of the Gábor Lázár-alike lead single 'Yokai', the album shifts into drive with 'Debris', reaching a jazzy apex on the discordant (and surprisingly cinematic) standout 'Noir'. We're sure you're tired of hearing the word "microtonal" at this point, but there's no denying the charms of a good xenharmonic scale when it's deployed so expertly.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由制作人Church Andrews与打击乐手Matt Davies合作完成，定位为高度实验性的电子声响作品。核心特色在于微分音/xenharmonic音阶的系统运用，将有机鼓击的即兴质感与精密的编程算法声响深度融合，节奏结构异常复杂。评论将其与Rian Treanor、Aleksi Perälä、Eli Keszler、Squarepusher等先锋电子艺术家并列，创作源头追溯到Terry Riley、John Coltrane与J Dilla的影响脉络。专辑在不同曲目间展现多面性：有的段落如失准唱机般令人不安，有的则呈现出接近Gábor Lázár的精密时钟感，而'Noir'一曲被特别提及为融合不协和性与电影感的亮点。整体横跨先锋电子、实验爵士与当代作曲多个领域，是面向小众深度听众的声响探索之作。

items.body:
Dead strong etheric elisions of chamber-jazz, trip hop and dream-pop from Bristol’s Tara Clerkin Trio, following up their acclaimed self-titled debut with a new EP of subdued but glowing reveries somewhere between Dominique Lawalrée's intimate parlour music, Third Eye Foundation's atmospheric configurations and the sort of skewed pop we'll always associate with the Laika x Moonshake axis. 

The effortless drift of ’In Spring’ is the trio’s 2nd vinyl release after 2019’s eponymous debut and a tape with Dublin’s Weeding in 2020. It’s a distinctly Bristolian affair in its beatdown pacing and smoky atmosphere, which the label themselves compare to the roster orbiting the city’s Planet Records (Flying Saucer Attack, The Third Eye Foundation) in the ‘90s, with hints of a less noirish Portishead, or the sweeter ends of the Young Echo sound.

'Memory' dissolves into the atmosphere, all muted woodwind and organ moans that erupt into a half-time drum warble; if trip-hop is back in 2021, "In Spring" recalls the genre's most low-key and thus enduring moments, while harmonizing with the wyrd-world narco-pop abstraction of contemporary forces Cucina Povera and Leila Sakini. 

Their elegant chamber sashay ‘Done Before’ carries Tara’s vocals on beautifully buoyant string and piano phrases trimmed with a sort of tripped sensibility, and ‘Night Steps’ pushes that aspect with crushed drums and filtered vox that feel like Teresa Winter on a Portishead track, and their nuanced range finally reaches into a sort of modal, 4th world lounge style recalling Julia Holter via Air on the impessively accomplished title tune. 

A quietly brilliant, memorable record >> Tipped!
items._cn_summary: 布里斯托尔三人组合的第二张作品，将室内爵士、trip-hop与梦幻流行融合为氛围感强烈的抽象声响。专辑延续了九十年代Planet Records厂牌（Flying Saucer Attack、Third Eye Foundation）以来的实验脉络，融合了Dominique Lawalrée式的私密室内乐语汇与Young Echo场景的烟雾感审美。曲目中可见木管与管风的低吟、弦乐与钢琴的轻盈对话，以及被电子化处理的人声与破碎鼓机节拍，整体在梦幻流行与前卫实验之间游走，并融入'第四世界'模态漫游的元素。与Cucina Povera、Leila Sakini等当代实验音乐人气质相近，属于安静而具探索性的跨界作品。

items.body:
Of all Jan Jelinek’s formidable output, this album has always been the one for us. More resolved and driven than 'Loop-Finding Jazz Records' (which appeared two years later), less reliant on glitch than Farben, it was essentially Jelinek's most satisfying and complete prototype for a new kind of sample-based music deeply immersed in the spirit of Jazz, without making any direct reference to it. 

Originally released via Move D’s Source imprint back in 1999, 'Personal Rock' is situated somewhere between 'Loop-Finding Jazz Records', his Farben output, and Move D's Conjoint work, full of subtle production flourishes sliding around deep House structures that belong to pre-millenial IDM, but which transcend its overly-fussy, masculine templates.

The music is brooding and full of romance, designed for late night immersion and bolstered by what we reckon is the most forward thinking and timeless production of Jelinek’s output over the last two decades. Impossible to pull highlights, it’s an album best experienced from end-to-end through multiple listens, drawing you into its quietly euphoric, blue mood.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是德国电子音乐家Jan Jelinek以Gramm名义于1999年发行的采样音乐作品，融合了爵士精神、微声/故障电子与深度浩室的结构。评论将其定位为Jelinek最具完成度的原型之作，介于其后续'Loop-Finding-Jazz-Records'、Farben项目与Move D的Conjoint作品之间，呈现出内省、浪漫、适合深夜聆听的蓝色情绪氛围。整体声响设计超越千禧年前IDM的繁复模板，以简洁的循环采样和微妙的制作手法构建一种安静的欣快感。该作由Move D的Source厂牌发行，属于独立电子/实验场景中的小众作品，文章对其在Jelinek创作脉络中的重要性给予了高度肯定。

items.body:
Magnum opus-weight album from organist and electro-acoustic composer Anna von Hausswolff, the entire record consists of just one instrument - the pipe organ, and represents absolute liberation of the imagination. It's a masterwork of gothic classical beauty - a must check for fans of Kali Malone, Kara-Lis Coverdale.

‘All Thoughts Fly’ was recorded at Gothenburg’s Örgryte New Church  and is heavily infused with the space’s atmospheric nuance, which renders the theatric richness of Anna’s compositions at their most billowing and melodramatic. As her 6th album, it’s also her most confident and strikingly original, following the slow steady procession of her sides for Kning Disk, Touch and City Slang with her most sepulchral and steepled refinement of black metal atmospheres and sacred dirges pronounced with an apocalyptic classical grandeur and iconoclastic experimental daring.

“Notes on the recording process: The organ on All Thoughts Fly is situated in Gothenburg and is a Swedish replica of the Arp Schnitger organ in Germany. It is the largest organ tuned in Quarter-comma meantone temperament in the world. With it’s four manuals, one pedal and 54 stops, it was built as part of a ten-year research project reconstructing 17th Century North German organ building craft. The tuning temperament is an important detail to note here, as it deeply affects the sound and tuning, and thus radically changed the process of creating this album. Anna speaks of a pleasant surprise during recording, the organ's ability to create beautiful "pitching" notes through its stops and air supply system. She remarks “We took advantage of this so most of the pitching sounds and notes that you hear on the album comes from the mechanics of this organ, effects made entirely acoustically." The organ was recorded with two room mics for atmosphere and two pairs of close mics placed inside the organ to capture nuances and detail for further organ sound processing by Filip Leyman in his studio.”
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由管风琴演奏家兼电声作曲家安娜·冯·豪斯沃尔夫创作，仅以管风琴一件乐器完成全部录制，作为其第六张专辑展现出高度的原创性与自信。作品在哥德堡的Örgryte新教堂录制，使用全球最大的四分之一音等律调音管风琴（17世纪北德管风琴工艺的复制品），将哥特式古典美学、黑金属氛围与神圣挽歌融合为宏大的声响景观。管风琴机械结构本身产生的独特"pitching"声效被巧妙捕捉，所有音效均为纯声学手段实现，具有鲜明的实验性与电声思维。专辑横跨当代古典、前卫实验与暗黑美学三大领域，与Kali Malone、Kara-Lis Coverdale等当代实验音乐家风格相呼应，是独立厂牌City Slang与Kning Disk旗下的高水准小众作品。

The idea for the set had come from artist and producer Erfen and sound engineer and percussionist Springer, two close friends who, taking advantage of cheap rent and disused buildings, put on regular events and established a recording studio in their neighborhood, off the beaten track. items._cn_summary: STROOM厂牌推出的这张合辑聚焦1994至1996年间旅居德国科隆的乌克兰地下音乐人作品，收录了Svitlana Nianio、Michael Springer、Guido Erfen、Soloveyka等艺术家的实验声响。评论追溯了1993年那批科隆边缘音乐场景的缘起：两位好友利用低廉租金和废弃空间建立录音工作室并举办定期活动，形成了独特的东欧地下实验社群。该合辑展现了乌克兰流亡音乐人与德国地下场景的交融，涉及氛围、电子、前卫即兴等多元领域，是后苏联实验美学与西欧地下文化碰撞的珍贵历史文献。

items._cn_summary: Shackleton 是一位以实验电子与低音音乐为核心的英国艺术家，此张专辑延续其近年来迷幻、原始且带有世界音乐色彩的声响探索路线。作品被描述为专为大型音响系统设计的低音向舞曲，融合了dubstep根基、迷幻质感与远古/未来交织的氛围美学。乐评提到他此前与多位实验音乐人（包括自由即兴吉他手与迷幻民谣艺术家）的合作脉络，暗示这张专辑延续了其跨领域融合的一贯路径。整体定位于地下实验电子场景，强调声响设计的物理冲击感与文化语汇的杂糅，非主流商业发行，适合对实验电子、低音文化与跨文化声响融合有持续关注的听众。

items.body: Alan Trench (Orchis, Temple Music,...) en Martyn Bates (Eyless in Gaza, Sorry For Laughing) zijn al sinds 2000 bezig met dit samenwerkingsverband en vonden sedert 2018 onderdak bij het eigenzinnige Italiaanse Final Muzik label. Sedert die tijd reviewen we hier ook bij Dark Entries de eigenzinnige, vaak conceptuele en andersoortige muziek van dit uitzonderlijk duo die beiden een verleden kennen in meer industriële en experimentele muziek. In Twelve Thousand Days, trekt de band veel meer de kaart van de donkere, avant-garde folk, ietwat vergelijkbaar bij wat je soms op albums van Current 93 hoort om een ietwat meer gekende naam in deze review te gooien, luister maar een keer naar “Asphodel Flowers”. Alle songs zijn als het ware op zichzelf staande verhalen die allen samen ook weer een goot verhaal vormen. Vol mysterie, een soortement ‘spleen’ (lichte depressie) maar dan wel eentje met oog voor natuur en schoonheid in de tristesse. Met deze “As The Moon Draws The Tide” is Twelve Thousand Days al aan zijn negende album toe, nu ja al, de groep is reeds actief sedert 2000 dus dat aantal valt in al die jaren enigzins mee. De sfeer van het album wortelt in de Briste traditie van mythologie en poëzie, het geluid is eerder minimalistisch en bij tijden zelfs breekbaar, met de ‘klagende’ stem van Martyn Bates in de hoofdrol. De akoestische gitaren woren ondersteund door sporadische percussie, orgel en her en der meer elektronische ambient aandoende soundscapes. Ze geven de nummers een wat bevreemdende, geheimzinnig sfeer die als het ware een soort natuurlijke adem is doorheen dit album dat ook door liedhebbers van pagan folk zal worden gesmaakt. Met Twelve Thousand Days komt als het ware de Briste folk traditie samen met de meer donkere post industrial scene waar beiden heren ook hun sporen in verdienden. Dit album, hoewel de zomer voor de deur staat, representeert eerder de korter wordende avonden en het verval dat in het herfstseizoen zijn magische intrede doet. Om dit album te kunnen appreciëren dien je tijd te maken, en je ergens op een knusse plaats te installeren, kopteloon op je hoofd en weg dromen. Op de digi-pak zijn tevens alle teksten afgedrukt waardoor je in de nummers kunt meeglijden zonder je suf te denken over wat er nu precies wordt gezegd / gezongen. Melancholie is altijd een beetje pijnlijk, dat is een beluistering van deze “As The Moon Draws The Tide” ook, maar zoals eerder gesteld, in tristesse baadt ook schoonheid, luister maar een keer naar songs als “Notes From A Ruined City” (zie clip), “Upon The Blasted Heat” , “ Ghosts” of “ Heathen Dog”. Twelve Thousand Days (facebook)
items._cn_summary: Twelve Thousand Days 是由 Alan Trench（Orchis）与 Martyn Bates（Eyless in Gaza）组成的长期合作项目，新作为其第九张专辑。音乐定位为暗黑前卫民谣，融合布里斯托尔的民谣神话诗歌传统与后工业暗潮底蕴。声音设计极简且脆弱，Martyn Bates 的哀歌式人声为绝对主角，原声吉他搭配零星打击乐、管风琴与电子氛围音景，营造出神秘异样的氛围感。专辑在悲恸与美感之间取得平衡，既适合 pagan folk 听众，也契合暗潮与后工业乐迷的审美。发行于意大利独立小厂牌 Final Muzik，保持着地下与实验音乐的纯粹气质。

items.body: By Matty Bannond Up to 35 percent of adults in the US have symptoms of insomnia (according to a 2025 study ). But those people’s night-time struggles vary significantly. They may have difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep or returning to sleep. Patients can suffer short-term or chronic afflictions. And the condition can be linked to anxiety, depression, chronic pain or other conditions. This twelve-track album by improvising saxophonist Andy Haas expresses the peculiarities of those various bedtime hardships—from overactive synapses and hyperactive fingertips to loneliness, self-pity and despair. It was recorded on the Winter Solstice of 2025 and presents Haas alone with his saxophones, as well as a Nano Pulsar pedal that chops, splits and reshapes his instrument’s sound. Nifty pedalwork opens up an expansive spectrum of manipulated outputs. Several tracks feature duplicate voices that suggest Haas talking to himself in the twilight. “Heart Less” involves two long-note drones that start at opposite ends of the saxophone’s register and meet in the middle. “This Dark Land” uses a similar technique, with voices helixing around a central pattern of changing pitch. Bursts of sound and oscillating frequencies are also common textural tricks. On “An Attenuated Goodbye”, a bluesy initial passage flits from singing to silence and back again. “The Cold Inside Us” has a piercing, car-alarm quality. Both pieces remind the listener of nights where a painful incident from the past refuses to subside or a concern about the future declines to wait until morning. Amid the midnight misery, there is a playful property to this thirty-minute experiment. In general, Haas tends to favor the higher register of his instrument. This adds a squeaky cheekiness to tracks like “Sense Less” and “Sleep Less”. His playing has a more noodly nature here, like a person exploring the liberating options that become available when the rest of humanity is in the sack. In Praise of Insomnia balances tonal and textural variety with recurring motifs, methodologies and moods. Although Andy Haas is a detail-driven artist, his improvisations often express a light-humored and capricious temper. This album is unlikely to help anybody fall asleep, stay asleep or return to sleep. But it might coax their mind down intriguing paths while they navigate restless hours in the day or the night. The album is available on CD and as a digital download  here . In Praise of Insomnia (2026) by Andy Haas   Subscribe
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由即兴萨克斯演奏家Andy Haas独自完成，仅凭萨克斯与Nano Pulsar效果器踏板构建出十二首作品，片长约三十分钟。音乐以自由即兴为骨架，融入电子声响处理与实时信号操控技法，如长音持续、倍频分裂、频率振荡等，拓宽了萨克斯的音色光谱。概念上以失眠的多重体验为切入点，涵盖神经亢奋、孤独、忧郁与冥想等夜间心理状态。部分曲目在高低音域间游走并螺旋交织，形成具有空间感的声学对话。整体风格处于学院派自由即兴与实验电子的交汇地带，演奏兼具技术细节与即兴直觉，对偏好前卫即兴与电子融合的听众具有较高吸引力。

items.body:
Following up 2021's Additive Inverse, Jim O'Rourke & Jos Smolders come together again for more sonic experimentation and procedural processing with Albumin. Their second on Moving Furniture, these two tracks showcase Jim's Kyma System generating the basis of the album before both he and Jos altered them separately in their studios. The result is a shimmering and ambulating collection of textures that flows, drifts, and pulls the listener into its midst to carry them forth through the duo's process. Working very well together, the pair combine sounds to form an enigmatic sonic stew, unpredictable and enjoyable, collected and concentrated.

Albumin's two pieces, "(HP)-(HP)" and "r(OP-OP)" are interesting in that they're a mix of disquiet and comfort, but somehow at the same time. This may be due to the way they curl and flow, feeling very organic despite their very synthetic genesis. Each texture and tone encapsulates the duality that exists in us that we cannot avoid putting forth in all that we encounter. We have our own Jim and Jos deciphering the output of the real Jim and Jos, and each playthrough affects the listener differently. Albumin plays like a soundscape, but not in the traditional sense. To me, it's like flowing down traces on a circuit board taking everything in; the green of the board replaces the grasslands and the copper traces become glowing rivers. To me, the sounds look like Tron meets Lion King. The highs and feedbacking pieces effectively pierce through the drones from time to time, catching the listener off guard, adding to that sense of disquiet. Albumin isn't harsh by any means, but the fiery stabs serve to remind the listener that even the safest environs carry some inherent danger. As stated above, each playthrough of Albumin affects the listener differently. Mood, volume changes, atmospheres, whatever changes give the play a life of its own. I think this is due to the varying strengths of the sounds in the mix, some being obscured by a distant hum behind you, let's say, leading to a more jarring listen, or getting the full range with headphones and eyes closed. It's definitely an intriguing album; the output is very cared for and it shows.

Jim O'Rourke & Jos Smolders show how two artists half a world apart can truly collaborate with their second release, Albumin. Stimulating, intriguing, and constantly moving, the album flows and changes, each piece part of a greater whole while still having its own voice. Coherent and collected, this bit of experimentation shows the duo's focus and drive to create pieces that are complete but still allowing the edges to be seen. Growing and changing with each spin, Albumin is a cool album that will get many plays.
items._cn_summary: Jim O'Rourke与Jos Smolders合作的第二张专辑《Albumin》，延续了两人基于Kyma系统程序化生成声音、随后各自在工作室独立处理的远程协作模式。专辑包含两首作品，呈现出流动、漂浮的质感纹理，在不安与舒适之间游走。声音虽源于合成器与算法，却带有强烈的有机感，融合了氛围音乐、drone、即兴与电子声响设计的元素。评论将其比作电路板上的河流穿梭，高频反馈不时刺穿持续的嗡鸣，形成张力的对话。整张专辑在小型独立厂牌Moving Furniture发行，体现了两位艺术家对实验声响的专注与匠心，适合偏好前卫实验与电子氛围融合的听众。

items.body:
Evidence lives up to its title very well. A lot of music in this fairly short album that makes itself heard with surprising simplicity.

EVIDENCE is a quartet: reeds, trombone, cello and drums. An unusual formation, but one that recalls Henry Threadgill's Zooid from 2015 onwards (without the guitar): In For A Penny, In For A Pound (Pi Recordings, 2015) and Poof. Sol Léna-Schroll (alto saxophone and clarinet) is Threadgill, Jørgen Bjelkerud (trombone) is Jose Davila, Joel Ring that of Christopher Hoffman, and Trym Saugstad Karlsen (drums) is Elliot Humberto Kavee.

The comparison goes no further. For here the music takes flight. The absence of piano and bass is turned to advantage in airy compositions and improvisations, whereas with Threadgill, drums and tuba (which Davila also plays) often take it upon themselves to bring everyone back down to earth. It is a feat of Karlsen's to breathe pulses that propel the music into the air.

Léna-Schroll and Bjelkerud are fellow members of Orchestra for Jazz Composers in Oslo / Orkesteret for Jazzkomponister Oslo (OJKOS) and L'Autre Collectif/Det Andre Kollektivet, a compelling initiative funded by France and Norway since 2019, where the innovative aspects of jazz and sometimes contemporary music are explored, and from which the label Autres Records was born. Bjelkerud and Karlsen appear in Amalie Dahl's Dafnie EXTENDED Live at Moldejazz, Ring in Eon, from Karoline Wallace's quintet, and Karlsen in The Aftermath (Fjordgata Records, 2026), of the major Ingeborg Gravem Sollid quartet, all almost simultaneously released. We are, in other words, at the very top of the tree.

The compositions and arrangements are precise and tightly structured. From them emerge improvisations in which the saxophone and trombone interlock in virtuosic spirals ("Mad Blue"). Freed from any earthly support, improvisation breaks free harmonically from the theme, while maintaining its formal rigour.

The brisk compositions would readily be described as bop in other circumstances, with perhaps a welcome Braxtonian touch. In particular, Léna-Schroll delivers a highly inspired solo in "Infinite Loop." The quieter pieces showcase the timbral contrasts, exemplified by an exquisite dialogue between Ring and Bjelkerud in "Infinite Fase."

This is an album of very high calibre with a great deal of substance. The lively and more measured pieces follow one another in a way that gives the album a fine balance. This beautiful, intelligent album is a breath of fresh air, an invitation to freedom, the opening of morning windows, and a day filled with positive energy.

Mad Blue; Infinite Down (#3); Band Music; Choral; Infinite Loop (#1); Infinite Fase (#2).

items._cn_summary: 挪威四重奏EVIDENCE以中音萨克斯/单簧管、长号、大提琴和鼓的非常规编制呈现这张专辑，完全摒弃钢琴和贝斯，使音乐获得罕见的轻盈与开放感。作品结构精密而严谨，编排紧凑，在此基础上展开高度自由的即兴对话，萨克斯与长号在螺旋式交织中展现精湛技艺。评论指出其兼具波普的明快节奏与Braxton式的先锋色彩，安静的段落则突显大提琴与长号的音色对话之美。乐队成员来自奥斯陆爵士作曲家乐团和法挪合作项目L'Autre Collectief，独立厂牌Autres Records发行。整张专辑在结构严谨与即兴自由之间取得平衡，展现了北欧当代爵士乐的前沿探索，定位为学术爵士与先锋即兴领域的佳作。

items.body: One of our top albums of 2025 receives the remix treatment, as Hymnal (Resung) highlights six of the original fourteen tracks. Visionary vocalist Lyra Pramuk is well-served by these new takes, which highlight facets of the works that might otherwise have gone unnoticed. Sequenced in a different order, the EP rearranges our perceptions of the original set, which we preferred to play as a single extended piece. Only “Ending,” for obvious reasons, remains where it was. “Unchosen,” the second track on Hymnal, is now the opening piece. The original began with vibrating synth, while Tarta Relena Aspre begins with Pramuk’s voice, heard as if approaching from a corridor. While the pieces end in a similar place, the remix extends the sonic distance traveled in a much shorter span. In contrast, Pramuk more than doubles the length of “Reality,” which in its 2:17 form seemed more of a bridge track. Adding a new percussive framework, the artist creates what seems like an entirely different piece, with greater vocal separation. The moody, experimental “Meridian” gains beats and a dance floor sensibility from Laurel Halo and John Tejada. Could this be Pramuk’s first charted single? We hope so; the remix opens the artist to an entirely new audience. In like fashion, the beats arrived late in the original “Oracle,” but enter immediately in the “Verraco Weightless Reshape,” with propulsive drums and a half-speed breakdown. The string-laden “Swallow” stays pitched-down and mysterious under the direction of Dumama, a miasma of sound with stuttering spoken word, disintegrating in its final moments like a computer glitch. And while the original “Ending” cannot be topped, “Djrum’s Endless Rework” wisely goes the alternative route, operating under a completely different set of rules. Operating as a series of movements, the piece goes from percussive stormer to subdued sampler to tribal hypnotizer to nearly-a cappella blanket, as uncategorizable as Pramuk herself. While the rework is not actually “endless,” it suggests that there is no end to the talent of the artist or to her potential trajectory. (Richard Allen)
items._cn_summary: Lyra Pramuk的实验性人声艺术作品《Hymnal》的混音EP版本《Hymnal (Resung)》，精选原专辑十四首中的六首进行重新诠释。Pramuk以极具前瞻性的人声技艺闻名，专辑横跨电子、氛围、人声实验与世界音乐融合的边界。混音阵容汇聚多位风格迥异的制作人：Laurel Halo与John Tejada带来舞曲节拍感，Verraco注入推进式鼓击，Dumama铺陈弦乐与迷雾声响，Djrum展开打击乐与部落催眠的层次。整体呈现出多面向的声响实验特质，从人声主导的走廊回响到舞蹈化处理，从破碎解构的spoken word到近乎无伴奏的绵延层叠，展现出极强的艺术张力和跨界融合能力。

items.body: The waters here are torrid. But the result of swimming in them is to emerge somehow richer than before. The sound of subtraction through propulsion: the old and archaic riotously stripped away to leave space for the new. A violent recalibration disguised as transcendence. A fearsome and unrelenting expression of archetypal metallurgy Kotra drops Dim Ren as a fearsome and unrelenting expression of archetypal metallurgy channelling brutalist ancestral mores through a facade of the teachings of Odin. “Travellers” opens the three-piece with pulsating bandwidth of abrasive sonic weaponry. Full force and face melting. It’s to experience noise music as a psychedelic and hallucinatory bright light, where distortion itself becomes ceremonial and ecstatic rather than purely confrontational. “Loose Braids” traverses the same sonic landscape but seemed to evoke a propulsion of greens and golds through the inclusion of a deeper tectonic intent. Rhythms feel partially unearthed from beneath collapsing industrial strata, carrying an atmosphere of ritual circuitry and scorched acceleration. And closer “Wren Calibration” is a-typical industriana in warcry mode. If you are brave and adventurous then dive in. The waters here are torrid. But the result of swimming in them is to emerge somehow richer than before. The sound of subtraction through propulsion: the old and archaic riotously stripped away to leave space for the new. A violent recalibration disguised as transcendence. Magical. Dim Ren is available on Prostir. [Bandcamp] Dim Ren by Kotra
items._cn_summary: Kotra的《Dim Ren》EP是一张工业噪音与仪式感融合的实验作品，在乌克兰独立厂牌Prostir发行。三首曲目以高密度的粗糙声波为基调，将失真与噪音转化为仪式性、迷幻性的体验，而非单纯的对抗性噪音。音乐中融入了北欧奥丁崇拜与祖先暴烈美学的意象，节奏如同从崩塌的工业地层下被挖掘出来，兼具原始仪式感与现代工业电路的冷峻。整体风格在暗潮/工业范畴内具有强烈的实验性与跨文化融合特征，将金属质感的声音锻造术与异教精神内核结合，展现出独特的暴力美学。适合偏好极端工业噪音、仪式音乐及前卫声响设计的听众。

items.body: Beim Duo Alan & Jan handelt es sich um die Produzenten und Klangkünstler Alan Abrahams, der unter anderem schon als Portable und Bodycode in Erscheinung trat, und Jan Jelinek, der seit über 25 Jahren seinen idiosynkratischen wie mikrotonalen Klangteppich knüpft und damit wohl ein eigenes Genre begründete. Take Me I’m Yours, die erste Zusammenarbeit der beiden, ist von der Cover-Art bis zum letzten Ton ein Collagen-Kunstwerk, wie es im Buche steht. Abrahams’ Songskizzen und verschiedenste Vokalspuren schickte dieser für einen Manipulations- und Produktionsprozess der besonderen Art an Jelinek, dessen abstraktes elektronisches Sounddesign sehr gut als Kontrapunkt zum organischen Klang der Stimme funktioniert. Mal geht Jelinek dabei recht rigoros vor und verfremdet die Stimme bis zur Unkenntlichkeit oder pitcht sie auf Zeitlupe herunter (»Together«). An anderer Stelle wird Alans Stimme zu gespenstischen Chorälen gelayert wie in »Window (Elpis)«. Im frühen Album-Highlight »Forever« hört man sogar eine nahezu klassische Gesangsperformance, inklusive Melodie und Text. Meist sampelt Jelinek aber nur für Sekundenbruchteile und benutzt Abrahams’ Stimme als organische Klangquelle, aus der er dann selbst kleine Melodien, Flächen und sanft pulsierende Beats bastelt. Abstrakt und doch geerdet entsteht auf Take Me I’m Yours aus vielen kleinen, subtilen Sounds ein großes Gesamtbild, das zwischen den zwei Welten von Alan und Jan vermittelt – und dabei eine dritte entstehen lässt.
items._cn_summary: Alan & Jan是两位电子实验音乐人的首次合作：Alan Abrahams（曾以Portable和Bodycode之名活动）提供人声素材与歌曲草稿，Jan Jelinek（以其微观电子声响设计闻名逾二十五年）对其进行了抽象化的处理与重构。整张专辑呈现出拼贴式的艺术构思，Jelinek以碎片化采样手法将人声转化为有机声源，编织出微小的旋律、声景与轻柔脉动的节拍。有时人声被大幅变调、减速至难以辨认，有时被层叠为幽灵般的合唱群，个别曲目甚至保留了接近传统的歌唱表演。专辑在Abrahams的声乐质感与Jelinek的抽象电子设计之间取得平衡，既扎根于具象表达又趋于抽象，形成介于两者之间的第三种声音世界。整体风格属于实验电子与IDM的范畴，融合了人声实验、声音艺术与极简电子节拍。

items.body: Tomasz Lukowicz has already earned his stripes with his Fractal project, through which he has released a truckload of productions. With Replicant, he reveals another side of his skills, and on the debut album “Critical Point”, he delivers 11 compelling tracks. Replicant sounds very different — more like an experiment in which the operator takes us deep into his sonic laboratory, completely unleashing his creativity in sound design. He supports these experiments with slow rhythms and broken beats. Lukowicz reveals himself here as a true sound architect, showcasing an impressive sonic landscape. I particularly enjoy the depth he creates in his bass lines, as well as some of the space-like electro arrangements. The whole album remains entirely instrumental. A touch of vocals or sampling here and there would not have felt out of place, but “Critical Point” already stands firmly on its own. The album even contains a few minimalist gems that are simply impossible to ignore. This is the kind of release that would have appealed to fans of the Tympanik Audio label back in the day, but which has now found the right home on Aliens Production. Call it Experimental with a touch of IDM subtlety, or simply Electro freestyle — this debut album is certainly an intriguing discovery. (Rating:8). Listen to “Depressing Fate Of Humanity”: https://aliensproduction.bandcamp.com/track/depresing-fate-of-humanity
items._cn_summary: 波兰制作人Tomasz Lukowicz以Replicant之名发行的首张专辑，呈现出深度的实验电子声响设计理念。整张作品完全器乐化，围绕缓慢节奏与破碎节拍构建，融合IDM的细腻质感与electro的自由流动，在低音线条的纵深处理与太空感电子编排上展现出鲜明的个人风格。乐评将其与Tympanik Audio厂牌时期的暗潮实验氛围相提并论，称其展现了真正的声音建筑师特质。专辑中包含若干极简主义亮点，整体定位为兼具实验性与IDM微妙特质的电子乐探索，适合偏爱声响实验与电子解构的听众。由东欧独立厂牌Aliens Production发行，延续了地下电子音乐厂牌的审美取向。

items.body: Puerta Negra’s latest single Complejo de Victima (Victim Mentality), comes on as a scathing indictment delivered with immaculate control. It’s strict, stylish, and wired for confrontation. Here, the Portland duo of María Aguirre and Mark Arciaga treat body music as a blunt instrument with a brain attached to it, and this lead single from their Metafísica EP sharpens the blade without polishing away any vitriol. Sung entirely in Spanish, the track places Aguirre’s voice at the center of the damage, cool and cutting, while the beat lurches forward with the mechanical confidence of a machine trained on human spite. Musically, Complejo de Victima works from a lean EBM chassis and lets the parts rattle. Industrial funk pressure runs through the track, but it never loosens into party decoration. The electronics have a mutant bite, closer to a feverish factory floor than a club fantasy, while the broken rhythms keep shoving the body forward at odd angles. Oráculo references Cabaret Voltaire, new-beat mutations, and the contemporary EBM revival, showcasing themselves as a band pushing their musical heritage through clenched teeth. Directed by Zach Flanary, the official video keeps its world deliberately stripped down: black-and-white, high contrast, bodies under pressure, faces treated less as glamour objects than as evidence. Aguirre and Arciaga perform as if trapped inside the song’s own nervous system, caught between command and collapse. The mirror shots give the video its mean little genius. They bend the performance into something fractured without dragging it into cheap psychodrama. A face splits, a figure doubles, the eye gets tricked into watching the watcher, and the victim complex named in the title starts to feel less like a diagnosis than a room full of bad faith. There is no need for plot when the premise is already poisoned: accusation, self-pity, control, and the private theater people build around their own wounds. Watch the video for Complejo de Victima below: Metafísica is billed as the third chapter in Puerta Negra’s vision, following 2022’s Costo Humano and 2023’s Playa Sola, and Complejo de Victima feels like a hard pivot toward austerity, attack, and psychic compression. Severity can be seductive when handled with nerve. Listen to Complejo de Victima below and pre-order the vinyl (out June 12th from Oráculo Records) here. items.body: In Anthology, the debut EP by Glaswork, Joshua Elijah makes a departure from the sharper angles of his previous work with Inertia Her, entering a more severe, spacious register. The Paris-based artist, producer, mixing engineer, and photographer has carried over a certain discipline from his earlier work, but the gesture here is one of subtraction rather than expansion. Across five tracks, Glaswork strips song form down to pressure, pulse, and pallor, allowing ambient electronics, contemporary classical texture, and EBM-derived movement to meet in a place where precision becomes emotional. The record has the feel of architecture abandoned before occupancy: corridors of tone, low mechanical thuds, rooms implied by resonance rather than filled with ornament. Elijah’s use of analogue and digital processes gives the music a tactile instability, as if each sound were being handled while still warm from the machine. There are traces of Tim Hecker’s engulfing grain and CoH’s sleek austerity, but Glaswork’s instincts are more private, less grandly apocalyptic. He works in measured gestures, allowing a bass figure or a softened industrial pulse to appear, recede, and leave behind a kind of charged absence. “Anthology is the result of mixing analogue and digital processes and letting experimentation lead the way,” says Elijah. “…five tracks built from dark electronic textures, ambient space, and restrained rhythmic ideas, focused more on mood and atmosphere than structure.” The statement points to the EP’s central temperament. These pieces do not hurry toward resolution. They collect and disperse, gathering weight through proximity. A rhythm may suggest the body, but it rarely gives itself over to club logic; a synth line may gesture toward melody, then dissolve into a colder field of tone. Elijah seems uninterested in spectacle, choosing instead to let small details carry the burden of feeling: the grain at the edge of a drone, the blunt knock of a beat, the way a suspended note can seem to alter the scale of the room around it. The EP’s emotional force lies in that refusal of excess. Glaswork begins here as a project of concentration, one concerned with the drama of reduction, where darkness is measured, space is active, and silence becomes another instrument in the arrangement. Listen to Anthology below and pre-order the album here. items._cn_summary: Glaswork首张EP《Anthology》将环境电子、EBM律动与当代古典质感融合于五首作品之中，呈现出以减法为核心的美学策略。制作人Joshua Elijah以模拟与数字混合工艺构建声音的触觉不稳定性，低频机械脉冲与悬浮的合成器线条在稀疏的声场中交替出现。整体气质克制内敛，接近Tim Hecker的颗粒感与CoH的冷峻极简，但更偏向私密化的空间叙事，拒绝走向宏大叙事或俱乐部化逻辑。节奏暗示身体性却始终保持距离，旋律暗示旋即消融于更冷的音色场域。沉默被作为乐器纳入编排，黑暗以精确的计量方式存在，空间本身成为活跃的构成元素。这张作品在暗潮、工业电子与当代古典的交叉地带展现出鲜明的个人语言，适合偏好实验性氛围声响与结构减法的听众。

items.body: This New World CD is by my count the fourth or fifth edition in half a century of a record that should never go out of print. Julius Hemphill released it on LP soon after its 1972 recording on his Mbari label. (Its name is writ large on the original cover; his own name did not appear. New World adds it to the facsimile cover.) He distributed it himself, and not many copies circulated. The album came out to a larger world with the 1977 version in Arista/Freedom’s new music series, with a new and striking cubistic photo-montage cover by Dennis Pohl, and liner notes by Robert Palmer which told us a bit about the West African Dogon people, and about Fort Worth–reared St. Louis–seasoned Hemphill. Curiously Palmer never IDs the backbones of Hemphill’s backbeat, cellist Abdul Wadud and ex-Paul Butterfield, ex-Art Ensemble of Chicago drummer Philip Wilson. (He did mention Julius’ right hand, trumpeter Baikida Carroll.) Advance word of a sort had come the previous year, with the release of Hemphill’s Arista/Freedom Coon Bid’ness , mostly recorded in 1975. It included “The Hard Blues” left over from the 1972 session, a tune which added Hamiet Bluiett’s bari to the core tet. A 2011 (pricey) limited edition CD miniaturizing the Pohl/Palmer package was produced by International Phonograph’s late Jonathan Horwich, who remastered the program from the original tapes (which he then donated to the Hemphill estate), sensibly tacking on “The Hard Blues” as a bonus track. So does the New World version, which also sports new notes by Hemphill colleague/scholar/archivist Marty Ehrlich. The sound has been newly refurbished by Paul Zinman, cleaning up the raggedy/degraded tape ending of “Rites.” (I haven’t seen it, but there’s also a new Superior Viaduct LP edition of the original program/artwork, with notes by John Corbett.) Wadud’s cello voice is prominent on Coon Bid’ness ’ choogling “Skin 1” and “Skin 2,” but even with that album to whet a new Hemphill fan’s appetite, Abdul’s entrance at the top of Dogon ’s 15-minute opening/title track was a stunner. First time I heard it, 49 years ago, I fell in love with the album before Julius had sounded a note: Wadud’s grinding one-bar bowed-dyads ostinato turned cello into a big Delta blues guitar. Wadud wasn’t the first jazz cello player by a long shot, though earlier ones mostly treated it like a baby bass. Other improvising cellists cropped up in the 1970s – Diedre Murray, David Eyges, Tristan Honsinger, Tom Cora, Ernst Reijseger ... – with many more soon to come, but nobody brought earthy sensibility and downhome funk to intonation and frictive bowing like Wadud. “Dogon”’s grinder riff nestled in the cracks in Philip Wilson’s sparse 11/16 drums and cymbal tattoo (a 4+4+3 he found tricky to master and held onto, tight, for most of it). And then come the horns, alto and trumpet melded in unison, and occasional blue minor harmony, phrasing like a single entity – the yoked horns of World Saxophone Quartet coming. (WSQ was already active when Arista/Freedom’s Dogon came out.) That melody is a series of bluesy aphoristic phrases that build on what’s already unfolded, then atomizes into a series of exclamatory single notes. The overall structure mirrors that odd-meter bar: the main melody’s sections are 19, 11 and 13 bars long.) In practice the melody seems capable of infinite development, while leaving space for cello and drums to speak through. (The cello part’s built-in variations may outline the harmony, arco or pizz.) And then comes Hemphill’s alto solo over vamping. Ornette’s North Texas holler is somewhere in the distance behind it, but Julius’s tone is dryer and harsher, his blues-infused intonation more sour and pitiless, his wildly scouring line informed by the written material: it’s all of a piece. He boils over and keeps boiling. (Baikida eases into his spot – won’t compete with that.) The blues gets dehydrated and reconstituted. “Dogon A.D.” is all slow build; swifter “Rites” plunges right into the twisty melody; we’re in the thick of action from the opening seconds, fast but with no fixed tempo, its recurring hook (and opening) a couldn’t-be-simpler drop of a whole step. Thick is right: three-part harmony with cello as third horn, or sometimes as droning tambura. (If Ornette’s in there, it’s the roiling Crisis .) Baikida is especially effective darting behind Julius, blowing bugler’s commentary, reinforcing but never upstaging the boss’ alto. “Rites” is all coiled energy; when it flags, return to the head for a quick exit. For still more contrast, there’s the slowly unwinding “The Painter” for Hemphill’s bucolic sung-multiphonics flute (refreshingly un-Rahsaan-like), its melody both wide-ranging and sing-song catchy. Timing and articulation can be tricky – it’s not a line a part-time flutist writes for an easy layup. Wadud strums or picks rhythm; Wilson rustles; Carroll is as ever the loyal supporter, nimbly selfless, has chops to burn but keeps them in check. It’s the composer’s show, even without Hemphill’s name on the original cover. And then “The Hard Blues” with its stompy riffy head, looking directly ahead to (and featuring half of) WSQ, but also – with its achingly-slow-to-quick tempos and dense-to-lean textures, suite-like variety and scored interludes – to Henry Threadgill’s 1980s Sextett. Whatever else he did, Julius Hemphill (like other members of St. Louis’s BAG co-op) brought convincing funk to new acoustic jazz, and reaffirmed the blues as eternal wellspring. Timeless tunes, an original group sound, liberatory cello – their appeal does not wear thin. Ehrlich’s notes describe in detail a private video of an earlier performance of the “Dogon A.D.” suite including a first unrecorded movement. The quartet was Hemphill, Carroll, Wilson and pre-Wadud pianist John Hicks, on vibes, playing what I’ve always thought of as the idiosyncratic ‘cello part.’ I imagine this performance as something from an alternate universe, one where Hemphill never performed at Oberlin College in 1970, and never met and jammed with the cellist known to classical audiences as Ronald DeVaughn, and that earthy blue arco scrape never got to shake us to the core. Ideally Dogon A.D. and Coon Bid’ness should be reissued together, a definitive picture of Hemphill’s (and Wadud’s) music in early bloom. Rights to both are currently held by Germany’s DA Music. But both together are just too long to fit on a single CD. (With thanks to Marty Ehrlich for fielding various questions.) –Kevin Whitehead
items._cn_summary: Julius Hemphill的《Dogon A.D.》是1972年录制、2011年前后多次再版的自由爵士经典。专辑以15分钟同名开篇曲为核心，大提琴手Abdul Wadud以一弓双音持续低音（ostinato）将大提琴转化为蓝调吉他般的粗粝质感，与鼓手Philip Wilson的11/16稀疏节奏相互嵌合，中音萨克斯与小号以齐奏与蓝调小调音程交织。整体风格介于学术自由爵士与西非Dogon文化意象之间，既保留了前哥伦布式的仪式感，又充满布鲁斯式的泥泞即兴张力。Wadud的大提琴用法在爵士史上具有开拓意义，挑战了此前将大提琴视作低音提琴替代品的传统。发行经由Mbari、Arista/Freedom及New World等独立厂牌完成。

items.body: Air Signs rests at its distinct sound. Everything is pieced together very well, and all the noises, melodies, and synths are family—they all align track after track. Deschamps has a gift for cohesion. Even when he’s working with degraded loops, reversed recordings, and heavily processed guitar, nothing feels fragmented. Everything belongs. Dreamlike and reminiscent of ambient joy Air Signs by anthéne   Brad Deschamps has been quietly building one of the most consistent catalogs in contemporary ambient music. Working under the anthéne moniker, the Toronto-based musician has released extensively on Home Normal, Past Inside the Present, Whitelabrecs, and Constellation Tatsu, while also running the widely respected Polar Seas Recordings label. His collaborations with Ian Hawgood (as Rosales), Stijn Hüwels, and David Cordero have earned critical acclaim, and his solo work is known for its dusty, emotionally resonant guitar and synth-led compositions. Air Signs arrives on Dronarivm, a small independent label from the Netherlands focused on contemporary ambient, electroacoustic, and modern classical music. Each piece here feels very dreamlike and reminiscent of ambient joy. A very easy listen. Inspired by a hawk that landed right outside the window at Deschamps‘ workplace in a hectic area of downtown Toronto, the pieces are light and airy, reflecting the stillness of our natural surroundings in the midst of human-made chaos. Dronarivm has built a strong catalog over the years, releasing work from artists like Chihei Hatakeyama, bvdub, and o[rlawren], all mastered with care and presented in limited physical editions. “Starling” and “all a blur” are standouts here. “Starling” has such a beautiful build to it with subtle guitar noises. Deschamps processes his guitar loops with a Chase Bliss Lossy pedal and a Vongon Paragraphs filter, both creating unusual tones, overtones, and artifacts. He also makes heavy use of a Maneco 16 second delay for lo-fi forward and reversed loops. This approach to guitar processing is what sets Deschamps apart from more straightforward ambient guitarists—the loops are degraded, filtered, and stretched until they’re barely recognizable as guitar. Rather than letting the track fade out into nothing or meaninglessness, “Starling” adds meaning through a steady bassline that anchors the swells and melodies drifting above it. Creating haunting, otherworldly textures (in reverse) :: “All a blur” is where Deschamps uses backward recordings and noises for reversed melodies. Writing reversed melodies is a craft that’s both detailed and tricky. When you reverse a recording, the attack and decay of each note flip—what was a sharp pluck becomes a slow swell, and what was a fade becomes an abrupt cut. This means that composing in reverse requires you to think backward about how sounds will evolve. It’s not just playing something and hitting reverse; it’s imagining how the reversed version will sound and then recording the forward version in a way that creates the desired effect when flipped. Sometimes it works beautifully, creating haunting, otherworldly textures. Sometimes it doesn’t, the timing feels off, the melody doesn’t resolve the way you’d hoped, or the reversed artifacts distract from the composition. Deschamps fits this perfectly here. At its core, “all a blur” sounds nightmarish, but it really isn’t. The reversed elements create an unsettling undercurrent, but the piece never collapses into darkness. It’s tense without being oppressive. Air Signs rests at its distinct sound. Everything is pieced together very well, and all the noises, melodies, and synths are family—they all align track after track. Deschamps has a gift for cohesion. Even when he’s working with degraded loops, reversed recordings, and heavily processed guitar, nothing feels fragmented. Everything belongs. The mastering by Peter Andersson helps too, giving the release a warm, unified sheen that ties the six tracks together. Air Signs is limited to 100 copies on factory-pressed CD, packaged in a unique discbox slider case with a soft-touch finish. For fans of guitar-based ambient and electroacoustic music, this is a strong addition to both Deschamps‘ catalog and Dronarivm‘s growing discography. Air Signs is available on Dronarivm. [Bandcamp] Air Signs by anthéne
items._cn_summary: anthéne 是多伦多音乐人 Brad Deschamps 的个人项目，《Air Signs》由荷兰独立小厂牌 Dronarivm 发行。专辑以氛围音乐为基调，融合重度处理的吉他循环、倒放录音与合成器音色，整体风格梦幻轻盈，灵感来源于闹市区窗外停留的一只猛禽。艺术家使用 Chase Bliss Lossy 失真踏板、Vongon Paragraphs 滤波器与 Maneco 延时等设备，将吉他音色降质、滤波并逆向拉伸，形成几乎无法辨识为吉他的绵长音景。专辑展现出高度的内在凝聚力，亮点曲目《Starling》以沉稳低音线锚定漂浮的和声层，而《All a Blur》则通过精心设计的倒放旋律——将音符的起音与衰减翻转——构建出超现实的悬浮质感。整体定位为注重声音探索的当代氛围作品。

items._cn_summary: 本文介绍格伦·布兰卡第十三交响曲《幻觉之城》在纽约的再度上演，由雷格·布卢尔担任指挥。该作品为百把吉他编制的大型实验性交响作品，首演于2001年世贸中心，2001年6月的演出中其泛音穿透建筑空间延伸至城市街道。布兰卡作为美国实验音乐与极简主义脉络中的重要人物，其创作以极端的吉他编制、密集的不和谐音与声学共振实验著称。本文所涉内容横跨实验/前卫音乐与当代古典/现代作曲两大领域，与用户核心偏好高度吻合。文中对声音空间的描写暗示了作品的沉浸式聆听体验，泛音与城市环境的互动体现其环境音乐特质。遗憾原文摘录过短，信息量有限。

items.body: Review by sgtpepper — It's great that the band release a live album in this line-up incarnation. Essential pieces of the 73-74 era are included, one from the masterful debut album and even a packed jam "Asbury Park".There are many instrumental highlights but the interplay between the bass and drums is worth calling out. Bruford clearly enjoys a room for improvisation and Wetton's aggressive playing style complements the essential dynamic sound.I have the newer USA live version, which includes "Fractures" which I'm very happy to be included. The density, tension and guitar playing are magnificent, especially in the ominous end.To sum it up, the material and playing are excellent but one would hope for a better overall sound (even though the instruments are distinctive) and greater length ;)
items._cn_summary: King Crimson于1975年发行的现场专辑，记录了乐队1973-74年阵容的演出实况。这是一张融合前卫摇滚与即兴演奏的作品，收录了首张专辑中的经典曲目以及较长的即兴段落"Asbury Park"。贝斯手Wetton富有攻击性的演奏与鼓手Bruford的自由即兴形成紧密互动，密度与紧张感贯穿始终，吉他演奏在尾声部分展现出压迫性的力量。评论者认为整体演奏与曲目编排质量优秀，但录制音质不够理想，且专辑时长偏短。

items.body: Following the previous album “Select”, which mainly featured a curated selection of tracks taken from Subverge’s existing releases, this new opus brings together a collection of unreleased, previously unknown, remix, and collaborative tracks. Henrik Karlsson personally selected the thirteen songs included here. There is perhaps slightly more diversity in terms of sound and influences on this record compared to Select, although the foundation of the compositions remains very much intact. Subverge continues to craft a highly distinctive form of Dark Ambient, occasionally enriched with slow rhythms and subtle percussion. Throughout the album, one can clearly hear Karlsson’s unmistakable fascination with Electro music and his irresistible urge for experimentation and sonic exploration. The result is a deeply cinematic work that, aside from a few vocal contributions, remains largely instrumental. Subverge excels at building dark atmospheres and allowing them to evolve gradually, much like the tension unfolding within a thriller film. Among the collaborations, the outstanding track with Access To Arasaka deserves special mention, serving as a true apotheosis of the album. Above all, Henrik Karlsson once again confirms his extraordinary talent for composing visionary and dark Ambient music, distinguished by intelligent sound design and remarkably refined production work. (Rating:8). Listen to “Purple Storm”: https://aliensproduction.bandcamp.com/track/purple-storm
items._cn_summary: Subverge的《Sequenced Suffering》是一张以暗潮氛围音乐为核心的器乐专辑，由Henrik Karlsson精心挑选十三首未发行、混音及合作曲目集结而成。整体风格延续了创作者标志性的暗黑氛围底色，融入缓慢节奏与细腻打击乐元素，同时展现出对电子音乐与声音实验的浓厚兴趣。作品具备强烈的电影感，暗黑氛围层层递进，犹如惊悚影片中逐渐积累的张力。与Access To Arasaka的合作曲目被特别提及为全作精华，在智能化声音设计与精致制作工艺上体现出创作者的扎实功力。专辑在保持暗潮根基的同时拓展了声场边界，是该领域一次稳健而成熟的呈现。

items.body:
Good Morning Tapes back with a new album of lushest New Age sound-bathing x emotionally gooey trip hop from Andro Gogibedashvili aka Saphileaum, delivered in a mode that’s highly tipped for anyone on the line from Enigma to All Saints, from a.s.o to Boards of Canada.

Saphileaum has spent the past decade in passage between notable houses of atmospheric sorcery - Mule Musiq, Not Not Fun, Slow Life, Constellation Tatsu - and of course Good Morning Tapes, who now host their 3rd meeting, ‘Heavenly Hills’. A definitive chapter in his ten year saga, it is flush with symphonic strings and sky born keys, breezily urged by percussion that straddles chill out and folk zones. That said there’s also a Balearic - or should that be Black Sea? - appeal to its title tune, that lingers in the glistening wake of ‘Your Grace’, to the shimmering breaks of a parting piece ‘Alarko (Cosmic Eagle)’, falling into the space between Boards of Canada's cult-inspired hauntological nostalgia and Shackleton's hallowed ethno-dub.

“The tracks in the album were written with the inspiration of the kingdom of Shambhala in the Himalayas. I'm deeply fascinated and touched by it. Even the album title, holds the idea of its Heavenly nature and the tracks are like individual, elemental parts of it. The album is not a journey into Shambhala, but rather a play and a dance with its energy, image and presence in my world. Alarko (Cosmic Eagle) is dedicated to my grandfather, Temur Tsiklauri, and I dedicate the whole album to my country Georgia, which I deeply love.”
items._cn_summary: 格鲁吉亚制作人Saphileaum在独立厂牌Good Morning Tapes发表的新专辑，定位为新纪元氛围声响与Trip-Hop的融合之作。音乐以交响化弦乐与天空感键盘为骨架，节拍横跨缓拍驰放与民间律动之间，标题曲带有地中海岛屿与黑海区域的明亮气息。整体声响在Boards of Canada式的怀旧电子回响与Shackleton的民族-低音之间寻找平衡，专辑灵感源自喜马拉雅香巴拉王国概念，并向艺术家故乡格鲁吉亚致敬。作品横跨电子氛围、世界音乐与实验弛放多个领域，具备跨类型融合特征和东欧高加索地区的文化视角，契合用户对电子与世界音乐类别的偏好。

items.body:
This is pure class! Bobby Ingham’s darkly cinematic debut LP seriously strikes a nerve for admirers of Space Afrika, Mark Leckey, Burial & Low End Activist with its evocation of life in C.21st West Yorkshire manifest in a tensely paranoid, homesick patch-work of knifed samples wrapped up in weightless grime & UKG structures

‘Angel Of The North’ inarguably hits a high water mark of Sneaker Social Club’s retro-futurist UK fixations with a deeply impressive demonstration of sound design tekkerz at the service of immersive, narrative-driven impressionism. For 30 mins the 24 year old Ingham belies his yung years with a grasp of melancholic pathos, atmospheric subtlety and articulate crud that one may expect from an artist years his senior. He effectively has us rapt front to back, from the frisson of noctilucent pads and dread subs in ‘Lynne’ to the lush resolution of ‘I Can’t Believe It’, hustling listeners heavy into what the label term a “social-realist inversion of sound system music that relishes negative space while telling a street-level story.”

That story is most suggestively limned via judicious sampling from a mix of personal and public archives, diffused across a spectra of ghostly, ephemeral arrangements perfused with flashes of the music he grew up with; from snatches of Wonder & T2 in the chamber grime abstract ‘Easy Mush’, thru skipping UKG reduced to Burial-esque degrees on ‘WYD Tomorrow Night.’ But it’s the poetic sense of restraint and sensuality that practically makes it a spiritual successor to label boss Low End Activist’s own evocation of life growing up on Oxford council estates (‘Hostile Utopia’ & ‘Municipal Dreams’), and clearly comparable to Mark Leckey’s collaged art-film soundtracks as much as the northern romanticism of Space Afrika’s liminal ambiance, or even EXLRUTH’s chamber adaptations of makina in its dare-to-differ approach and spellbinding effect. 

Big tip!
items._cn_summary: Bobby Ingham首张专辑以黑暗电影化的声音设计为核心，将grime与UKG的节奏骨架解构重组，融入大量拼贴采样与负空间运用，营造出沉浸式的叙事氛围。整体风格介于ambient、IDM与dark ambient之间，声响层次丰富，氛围阴郁而克制，带有社会现实主义的叙事视角。专辑将低音系统音乐反转，削弱打击感而强化空间感与情绪张力，在chamber grime与ghostly ambiance之间找到平衡。独立厂牌Sneaker Social Club发行，与Space Afrika、Burial等UK地下电子传统一脉相承，展现出年轻创作者在声音设计上的成熟度与艺术个性。

items.body:
Donato Dozzy and Neel's critically lauded 2012 opus is re-pressed for 2026, highlighting just how influential it's been in the years since,

If you're into psychedelic, trance-inducing minimal techno, then you've probably come across Voices from the Lake already. If not, then prepare yerself for an interface with yr new favorite album. Released over a decade ago, the record made an immediate connection with clubgoers searching for a lysergic alternative to minimal's booming, avoidant monotony. Dozzy and Neel approach their tracks with enviable restraint: kick drums are present on the self-titled album, but forced into submission, not dominating the tracks but occasionally adding punctuation to their whirling structures. The key to each segment - which run into each other to form a longform heat haze of abstract percussion and offworld sound effects - isn't the drums exactly, but the mood the two Italian veterans are able to extract using only the most spartan ingredients.

The elements are familiar - cycling melodic phrases, distant pads, unstable rhythms - but the way Dozzy and Neel assemble them feels human and connected. On 'Iyo' there's barely a chance for the track to develop into a proper banger; all tension, no release. Elsewhere on 'Manuvex' the kick is softened into a damp thud, left to underpin shivery Porter Ricks-esque glitches and peculiar, dissonant synthetic elements that breathe with rare humanity. With the shortest track weighing in at a generous seven and a half minutes, and the longest hitting 16, it's an epic that's not afraid of simmering in its own juices until it's fully cooked. Bit of a classic?
items._cn_summary: 这是意大利双人组Donato Dozzy与Neel于2012年发行的迷幻极简科技舞曲专辑，2023年再版。作品以克制手法构建长时间流动的声响空间，融合抽象打击乐、循环旋律、远距氛围铺底与不稳定节奏结构。专辑呈现出致幻与恍惚氛围，鼓机被弱化为沉闷点缀，glitch元素与不和谐合成器音色在七至十六分钟的长篇结构中缓慢展开。整体风格介于极简科技舞曲、ambient与实验电子之间，声响设计兼具冷感与人性化温度，在地下电子音乐领域具有相当影响力，是该流派公认的标杆作品之一。

items.body:
Bristol’s quietly revelatory Tara Clerkin Trio usher a magnificent new 30 minute mini album of folk-jazz and classical-downbeat chamber music x dreampop with their return trip for London’s World of Echo, hugely tipped if yr into Laika, Pram, Broadcast, Hydroplane, A.R. Kane, Portishead, Laila Sakini.

Effortless and transcendent, Tara Clerkin Trio unpick and rethread myriad 90’s DIY tropes on an undeniably genius new mini album that takes the brittle, asymmetric pop of Pram, Stereolab’s orchestral arrangements, A.R. Kane’s penchant for straight looped-Amen-dreampop, and drape it with esoteric and uncomproimisingly modern chamber jazz and baroque folk baubles that are just impossible not to fall deeply in love with.

Aye that title track is an instant wonder, and shares a 90’s undercurrent with the more dubwise ‘World in Delay’, where echoes of Laika’s hybrid vibrations surface to transport us to a different time. ‘Marble Walls’, meantime, manages to remind us of both Broadcast’s ‘Tears In The Typing Pool’ and Stereolab’s 'Cybele's Reverie', all sweeping orchestral flourishes urged by a daydreamy, bubbling rhythm. 

The rest catches them in measuredly introspective mode, tidily drifting along streams of ferric hiss, rippling marimba and accordion into a hazy fantasy like Don Cherry meets A.R. Kane on the downbeat slunk of ‘Brigstow’, and folding a lute riff into loopy origami on the glorious, pastoral fade to close of ‘Once Again’. 

Stunner.
items._cn_summary: Tara Clerkin Trio 来自英国布里斯托，发行了一张融合民谣爵士、室内乐、梦幻流行与电子元素的迷你专辑。整体风格建立在九十年代DIY美学之上，借鉴了Pram的棱角流行、Stereolab的管弦编曲、A.R. Kane的循环碎拍梦幻流行等元素，并融入巴洛克民谣与室内爵士的质感。乐器配置包括马林巴、手风琴、鲁特琴等，配以磁带嘶声与dub式节奏。作品在复古氛围与现代制作之间取得平衡，编曲层次丰富，既有沉稳内省的冥想段落，也有旋律明亮的展开。伦敦独立厂牌World of Echo发行，保持了地下音乐的自有脉络。该作品在实验性、爵士底蕴、跨界融合方面均与用户口味有较高契合度，但核心创新仍基于九十年代既有语汇的重组。
