items.body: If you want to be countedIf you want to be seenThen you can never be freeNot me Black Marble, the long-running solo project of synth musician Chris Stewart, will return this summer with Life in Small Spaces, his first full-length album since 2021’s Fast Idol. The record is due on August 21, 2026, via Sacred Bones, and its announcement comes with a new single, “Jim Carol New Year,” alongside a 16mm video directed by Clayton Hunt. The title carries a sly double meaning, nodding to author, poet, and musician Jim Carroll while brushing against the sing-song formality of holiday carols. The song itself is less festive than the name suggests, though it moves with a dry, almost buoyant touch. Stewart sets a rhythmic synth figure against a clipped, cool vocal delivery, letting the track drift between deadpan humour and a serious suspicion of authority, belief, approval, and all the social traps dressed up as advice. Jim Carol New Year casts a skeptical eye on the voices that claim authority over modern life: teachers, preachers, critics, experts, and anyone else selling certainty as salvation. Stewart turns the repeated phrase “I forgot my money” into a dry punchline and a philosophical dodge, as if the speaker has wandered into the marketplace of bad advice and left his wallet at home on purpose. The song treats public approval, easy belief, and social belonging as traps dressed up as rewards, while its brighter melodic movement gives the critique a sly lift. Beneath the humour sits a more personal bruise, with failed intimacy and self-recognition slipping into the frame, deepening the song’s argument about freedom, compromise, and the cost of being seen. “If you want to be free,” Stewart says, “you have to watch out for some of life’s classic pitfalls.” Black Marble has a gift for making private unease feel oddly aerodynamic, and Stewart applies that instinct to a song about doubt as self-preservation. The arrangement glides with a melody that carries the critique in clean lines instead of forcing the point. Its charm works as camouflage for a tougher thought: the desire to be recognized can become its own quiet trap. “Chris had an idea of a house in the distance with two travelers being drawn toward it,” director Clayton Hunt shares regarding the video. “We wanted each traveler to represent a different version of the journey. One traveler struggled unprotected against the landscape, the other was cautious, outfitted in an orange hazmat – type suit. I decided to shoot 16mm and capture everything against the green landscape, creating a vibrant contrast. That imagery helped guide the production and inform the story.” Hunt’s video gives the single a spare, strange visual frame. Rather than crowding the song with plot, the clip follows two travelers drawn toward a distant house. One moves exposed through the open landscape, while the other proceeds with caution in an orange hazmat-type suit. The image is simple enough to read in several directions: risk and protection, instinct and fear, faith and armor, two ways of moving toward the same uncertain promise. The 16mm format suits Black Marble’s current turn toward a more physical band-room feel. Watch the video for Jim Carol New Year below: Black Marble’s Life in Small Spaces finds Stewart trading some of his usual synth density for staccato guitar lines inspired by early American left-of-the-dial college radio, with reference points including Pylon, The Necessaries, and R. Stevie Moore. Live drum samples, informed by Wire’s clean metronomic economy, help shift the project toward a leaner, more tactile sound. Stewart describes the album as a record about the music industry, authenticity, and the question of how independent artists survive without surrendering the private logic that made the work worth making in the first place. “I always knew a lot of people in music struggled to make ends meet, but it surprised me to learn that the people you thought would be doing well often weren’t. For me, seeing the business from the inside like that changed how I looked at things. When I looked up to see a new artist on a billboard, I started to wonder, will I one day have to pretend to be something I’m not, in order to succeed? The life of an artist goes on after your moment ends, you know? So who do you want to be in the end and how do you want to be seen by the people that know you? I made Life In Small Spaces while thinking about that, and for me, it serves as my own ideal for living an artistic life. I’m doing it as a vocation, not some last ditch effort to escape to some other world. I made this record not only as a way of saying that, but as a way of saying it’s ok to feel that way. It’s ok for people to sacrifice some degree of creature comfort in order to live a life you believe in. And it doesn’t have to be an endless search for something just out of reach, it can be a permanent way of being and something that sustains you.” In that sense, Jim Carol New Year makes for a pointed first dispatch. Its melody may turn lightly, but its message keeps its composure: beware the expert, distrust the sales pitch, and save your freedom for something worth more than being seen. items.body: Re:Mission Entertainment has signed somemagicalshit, the bilingual synthpop and dark electronic project of Houston’s Courtnii Veronica Rose, with a debut full-length album set for release this fall. The announcement gives a proper label frame to a project already wired for bruised nerves, bad glamour, private panic, and the kind of synth damage that makes a bedroom feel like a pirate radio broadcast tower. Rose started somemagicalshit in 2022 as a solo operation: computer, synths, sequencers, and a skull full of voltage. By 2023, the project had grown into a full live band, which makes sense, because this is the kind of music that wants bodies dancing in front of it. It has Le Tigre’s art-damaged bite, TR/ST’s bruised electronic glamour, ADULT.’s stern machine-body snap, Pussy Riot’s bilingual agit-pop provocation, and the frostbitten drama of Kælan Mikla, all dragged through Rose’s own Houston heat and private hell. She writes, records, mixes, and directs the entire affair herself, building songs that feel glossy, unstable, wounded, and ready to throw a drink at the mirror. Я ненавижу себя moves between Russian and English as Rose calls herself ugly, rejects advice, declares therapy useless, reaches for alcohol as medicine, and circles the same brutal thought until it becomes a chorus: “Ya Nenavizyu Sebya.” The title translates to “I Hate Myself,” and the track treats that phrase with the blunt force of a diary entry written hard enough to tear the page. There’s face paint, jealousy, body disgust, and the desperate wish to love herself again, all carried by stacked synthesizers and vocals that cut through the arrangement with theatrical ache. The Russian lyrics give somemagicalshit a serrated emotional edge, bending the song’s pain into something harsher, stranger, and more intimate than plain English confession could manage alone. Rose’s voice moves from sneer to exposed nerve without getting coy about the damage, while the music keeps enough pop instinct to make the misery stick in your teeth. “The goal from the beginning was to create something atmospheric and emotionally intense while incorporating the beauty and emotion of the Russian language into alternative electronic music,” says Rose. “That mission hasn’t changed. It’s only getting louder.” The video for Я ненавижу себя, directed by Jorge Delgado, turns self-loathing into a public spectacle with a weird grin taped to its face. Rose performs with live-wire force while an audience watches from behind paper bag masks, reflecting the song’s shame. The clip has the charge of a basement show, a breakdown, and a prank pulled on the bad voice in your head all at once. “This is a song about suffering with self-hatred, making this video was a dream come true for me and I hope that you all enjoy it! It is slightly humorous as well as serious,” says Rose. Watch below: Houston’s alternative scene has already been getting the message, with short tours, out-of-town dates, and new material pushing the project beyond its original bedroom-bunker beginnings. With Re:Mission now behind it, somemagicalshit’s forthcoming full-length looks set to deliver a very stylish nervous breakdown with teeth. Catch somemagicalshit on the road in the America South this summer! items._cn_summary: 这是一张波斯古典音乐传统的专辑，由打击乐手Keyvan Chemirani领衔，延续了其家族Cheminrani Ensemble的传统。专辑以波斯古典音乐为核心，融合家族世代传承的打击乐技艺与传统波斯音乐结构。Cheminrani家族在中东和地中海音乐圈享有盛誉，常以独特的文化视角呈现伊朗传统音乐。该专辑在Songlines杂志获得关注，说明其在世界音乐领域具有一定的艺术价值。然而，由于乐评内容极为有限，仅一句话描述，无法判断其是否融入了实验性元素或跨流派创新，整体信息不足以全面评估其艺术深度和突破性。

items.album: IL CERCHIO D'ORO Pangea e le tre Lune (Rock Progressivo Italiano, 2023)
items.excerpt: Review by andrea — " Pangea e le tre lune" is the fourth album by Il Cerchio d'Oro and was released in 2023 on the independent Black Widow Records label with a line up featuring Franco Piccolini (keyboards), Giuseppe Terribile (bass, vocals), Gino Terribile (drums, percussion, vocals), Piuccio Pradal (guitar, vocals) and Massimo Spica (guitar) plus some prestigious guests such as Donald Lax (violin, from historic Italianprog band Quella Vecchia Locanda), Tolo Marton (guitar, former member
items.body: Review by andrea — " Pangea e le tre lune" is the fourth album by Il Cerchio d'Oro and was released in 2023 on the independent Black Widow Records label with a line up featuring Franco Piccolini (keyboards), Giuseppe Terribile (bass, vocals), Gino Terribile (drums, percussion, vocals), Piuccio Pradal (guitar, vocals) and Massimo Spica (guitar) plus some prestigious guests such as Donald Lax (violin, from historic Italianprog band Quella Vecchia Locanda), Tolo Marton (guitar, former member of Le Orme), Ricky Belloni (guitar, from Nuova Idea and New Trolls), Valerio Piccioli (guitar) and Carlo Deprati (narrative vocals) who contributed to enrich the sound. This album confirms all the good qualities of the band's previous works, with a sound deeply rooted in the seventies yet never overly nostalgic and a music always in service of the storyline. It's a concept alnum that tells of the birth of the Earth with fantasy and fairytale nuances. The lyrics are by Giuseppe Paolino, an old friend of the band, while the beautiful art cover is by Armando Mancini, a talented painter who's behind some seventies iconic prog album covers like those of Quella Vecchia Locanda...The title of the opener, "Pangea", refers to the supercontinent that existed during the late Paleozoic and early Mesozoic eras and began to break apart about 200 million years ago. After a dreamlike introduction with piano and flute in the foreground, the music and lyrics evoke a ball of fire that some god has carelessly hurdled into eternity. The music is dense and rich with shifts in tempo and atmosphere, while the lyrics, with nuanced tones, outline the mystery of creation. No one knows exactly how it happened, there are no witnesses, but the flame slowly turned into Earth. So, it's just a strange trick of fate that gave life, almost with childlike innocence, to this new entity that will become a continent and be called Pangea...In "Alla deriva" (Adrift) the music and lyrics describe the new continent floating on dark, restless waters, a lifeless land slowly drifting aimlessly across a frightening landscape. Three amused moons watch over it from the sky...Introduced by a dreamlike section with the violin in the forefront, "Dialogo" (Dialogue) evokes the image of a shooting star causing the fragmentation of the new continent. The fractured land turns to the wind and the moon, giving rise to an imaginary dialogue. The wind pushes Pangea onto the sea waves and lifts it to seek a new path, while a friendly moon watches from above and smiles, accompanying it into the darkness of the night..."Le tre lune" (The three moons) is a complex piece, rich in nuances and changes in rhythm and atmosphere. The music and lyrics evoke the image of three moons slowly revolving around the Earth. The first is red, the second yellow, and the third is black, blending into the darkness of the night. Each moon chases the other, casting colourful reflections on the sea of ​​Pangea. These marvellous reflections spark a dispute between the three vain moons. Eventually, the yellow and red moons implode and dissolve, leaving only the black moon in the sky of Pangea. Over time, the black moon learns to wear yellow and red colurs, while it tires of black and, from then on, wears it, albeit elegantly, only occasionally...The instrumental introduction to "Dal nulla cos�" (Out of nowhere, like that) might recall Le Orme, but the piece then develops in an original way. The music and lyrics describe a desolate and hostile landscape: a dark sea, brown earth, earthquakes and storms, winds and active volcanoes. Who would have thought that life could arise in such a place? Yet there was no past nor fear, and life began its journey toward an unknown future,...The next piece, "E la vita inizi�" (And life began), dreamily describes the beginning of life on Earth. Beneath a carpet of stars, Pangea continued its journey unstoppably, driven by a rebellious sea. The continent broke apart, then reunited, changing shape several times until reaching its current form. Chance, chemistry, and the sun's rays helped life emerge from the seabed, now less dark and threatening. An evolutionary process destined to never stop...The album's final piece, "Crisi" (Crises), is listed as a bonus track and has nothing to do with the concept. It's a hard rock song (with obvious references to Deep Purple) released as a single in 1981 and occasionally played by the band during their concerts. It deals with the economic crisis and social values ​​of the late 1970s...On the whole, an excellent work that should find a place in your Italianprog collection!
items._cn_summary: 《Pangea e le tre Lune》是意大利老牌前卫摇滚乐队Il Cerchio d'Oro的第四张专辑，2023年由独立厂牌Black Widow Records发行。乐队阵容以键盘、吉他、贝斯、鼓为核心，并邀请了Quella Vecchia Locanda、Le Orme、New Trolls等意大利前卫摇滚名团成员参与录制。专辑以盘古大陆分裂的神话叙事为概念，通过钢琴、长笛、小提琴的交织铺陈，描绘地球诞生与三颗月亮环绕的幻想场景。音乐风格深植于七十年代意大利前卫摇滚传统，节奏与氛围变化丰富，结构复杂且叙事性强，但整体仍属传统交响前卫范畴，未见明显实验声响设计或跨类型融合。该专辑在老派意式前卫领域延续了乐队的稳定水准，适合经典RPI爱好者，但对于追求前卫实验、当代作曲或电子声响融合的听众而言，风格较为保守。

items.body: Justin Taylor’s Clavecin XX presents an intriguing selection of solo and ensemble works by Bartók, Françaix, Górecki, Poulenc, and Manuel de Falla, placing a traditionally antiquated instrument squarely in a modern context. For this recording, Taylor utilizes a 1970s harpsichord by Anthony Sidey that hybridizes elements from 1920s Pleyels with much earlier models. This versatility, the artist notes, allowed him to rely on a single instrument throughout the diverse recital. Indeed, the Sidey instrument’s profile encompasses an array of personalities and sonorities that are brilliantly unveiled across the album. Clavecin XX Amazon Presto Apple Referencing Baroque forms like the Toccata and Minuet, Jean Françaix’s Concerto features a distinctive tonal language that places the harpsichord in a curious perspective. Deriving its energy from Taylor’s full-bodied tremolos, Toccata I is further animated by piquant string pizzicatos that add a sprightly, balletic quality. Sharing a similar texture but adopting a diametrically opposed, lyrical profile, Toccata II allows the keyboardist to trace horizontal lines with a pleasing legato, its fluidity highlighting refreshing harmonic progressions. Demonstrating the chameleon-like quality of the instrument, Taylor shines in the Minuet. Here, the harpsichord occasionally resembles a dulcimer or a Japanese koto, bringing a fitting dimension to a multifaceted compositional language steeped in Impressionism, cinema, and dance. Serving as a stark departure from the preceding charm, the selection by Henryk Górecki is deeply stimulating in how its two movements employ repetitional minimalism to cast the harpsichord in strikingly different lights. Taylor’s even-keeled perpetuum mobile in the Allegro molto is insistent, clashing unapologetically with the equally stubborn, static ensemble part. The resulting sonority is mechanical, bordering on the computerized. Driven by relentless chords, the subsequent Vivace marcatissimo builds profound tension. The performers do a remarkable job maintaining metronomic precision, molding a conflict that eventually comes to a head as spectacular harmonic collisions evolve into a frenetic sonic assault—an effect most certainly intended given the music’s inherent angst. While Manuel de Falla’s selection injects rhythmic vitality into the program, Francis Poulenc‘s Concert champêtre stands out for its high-spirited, imaginative execution. Written for Wanda Landowska (an artist Taylor cites as a major inspiration), the concerto operates in a Neo-Baroque style. Conjuring stately authority in their slow introduction, the orchestra sets the stage for the keyboardist to bring elegant liveliness to the Allegro section. The Finale is arguably the most engaging movement due to its sheer eclecticism. Launching as a virtuosic Gigue, it quickly diversifies to encompass hints of improvisation, a march, and elements drawn from Romantic and Neo-Romantic symphonies. Adapting to this complex structure admirably, the performers ensure no particular reference feels contrived or out of place. In this work, as in the other concertos, the Orchestre National de Lille under Chloé Dufresne is an attentive partner, articulating the clever counterpoint clearly while never overshadowing the harpsichord. Justin Taylor. Photo © Jean-Baptiste Millot. Turning to the solo works, the opening selection from Bartók‘s Mikrokosmos serves as a brief but wonderfully rendered introduction, establishing the character of the entire program through its interplay between consonance and dissonance. Taylor’s precise articulation gives the notes ample space to resonate, allowing listeners to appreciate them individually while sympathetic resonances beautifully mingle. Paying homage to György Ligeti’s landmark harpsichord work Continuum (which famously transforms the instrument into an ominous, persistent buzz), Stéphane Gassot’s Bluesinuum offers a gentler take. Although it references a similar trill-like texture in its middle section, Gassot’s approach is notably more subdued. Taylor’s bluesy rhythms possess both snap and fluidity, while occasional lower-register rumbles introduce a welcome playfulness to the mix. Concluding the album is a familiar tune: Scott Joplin’s Maple Leaf Rag. While the execution is solid and the artist’s transcription remains faithful to the original, hearing this piece on a harpsichord proves difficult to digest. The timbre of the instrument simply does not suit the repertoire, transforming the music’s inherent jauntiness into something rather heavy and labored. Perhaps this iconic rag is best left to its intended medium, the piano. Taylor’s interview in the liner notes portrays him as a well-spoken, meticulous musician who has invested significant research into his repertoire prior to performance. With the exception of the final track, this curation stands as an engaging testament to the harpsichord’s vast capabilities well beyond its traditional Baroque boundaries. Though not all the pieces make for easy listening, Taylor undeniably maximizes the instrument’s technical and musical capacity. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑收录了二十世纪作曲家巴托克、弗朗赛、戈雷茨基、普朗克和法雅为羽管键琴创作的作品，试图将这一传统古乐器置于现代语境中。演奏者使用一架1970年代由Anthony Sidey制作的羽管键琴，融合了1920年代普莱耶尔琴型与更早期乐器的特征，使单一乐器应对风格多样的曲目。弗朗赛的协奏曲借鉴巴洛克形式却运用现代和声语言，戈雷茨基的作品采用重复性极简主义手法，普朗克的《田园协奏曲》则属新巴洛克风格。整张专辑在当代古典范畴内展现了一定探索性，但整体仍偏向新古典与新巴洛克美学，与激进实验/前卫领域距离较远，更适合对当代古典羽管键琴文献感兴趣的听众。

items.body: With the cards you hold But who’s on trial Carve their names Declare your crimes Since we last checked in, Brooklyn-bred noise rock quartet Clone have been hard at work, honing their craft on stage and in the studio. The band has just returned from a short stint on the road and offer up a blistering video for single “Care to Try?” from their EP of the same name, which was released in October of last year. “Care to Try?” follows up the band’s debut album CL.1, released in 2024. “Care to Try?” is a powerful anthem of resistance, targeting and taunting the current political administration in the USA with biting lyrics and hard-hitting, guitar-driven discord. Opening with short burst of feedback and a catchy, yet incisive melody, the track quickly takes hold and goes straight for the jugular, with vocalist LG Galleon seething and shouting lyrics of rebellion above the din to dizzying effect. Shades of bands such as Live Skull, Naked Raygun, The Chameleons, and Killing Joke can be heard throughout the track, which eventually explodes into a cacophonous, scorched-earth coda that commands reflection and action. Filmed and colored by Devan Davies and edited by Galleon, the video for “Care to Try?” perfectly reflects the song’s fiery intent. “With their second go-around things just seem even more hopeless than before,” adds Galleon, “and this video tries to capture he frustration of an ever increasing world gone mad.” Check out the track and video below, and be sure to catch the band live this Thursday at Berlin Under A in NYC. More dates below. items.body:
After the cataclysm of their Om debut, Al Cisneros & Chris Hakius come right down with its hypnotic follow-up, now returned to circulation on its 20th anniversary FFO Sleep, Earth, Popol Vuh.

‘Conference of the Birds’ (2006) had big boots to fill after Om’s immense 2005 debut ‘Variations on a Theme’, so they effectively slipped into a pair of sandals instead, feeling the sand between their toes on a pair of more desert oriented jams. Still squinting at durational horizons, they take all the time needed - up to and over 15 mins per side - to concentrate on more brooding strains of modal, psych-inflected stoner rock that works it magic more subtly. 

The hairy nads-out appeal of their previous side, and the grungier tone of their earlier, cult work as Sleep is swapped out for mantric, pentatonic riffs and sway that channel the blues via Ethiopian music, kosmiche and hard rock in ‘At Giza’, placing Cisneros’ monotonic vox higher in the mix over shimmering backdrop of hazed hi-hats and uncurling bassline yoked with a tongue-tip tension.

But fret not heavy riff fiends, for that all comes with ‘Flight of the Eagle’, which effectively picks up where ‘Variation…’ left off, locking hard into a mantric cycle where Hakius’ damn slow but tight offbeat shuffles and the feedback worship riffs hold an intensity that breaks upward half way and soars in tumbling gyres to the end.
items._cn_summary: OM乐队由Sleep成员Al Cisneros与Chris Hakius组成，这张专辑将毒草石摇滚置于沙漠摇滚的基调之上，融入埃塞俄比亚调式元素、宇宙摇滚氛围（致敬Popol Vuh与Earth）以及冥想式五声音阶循环。Cisneros单调的念诵式人声漂浮在嗡鸣低音线与氤氲镲片之上，整体呈现出催眠般的长篇结构。专辑在毒草摇滚框架内做了跨界融合尝试，埃塞俄比亚音乐的影响为重型riff注入了异域色彩，而慢速反馈与调式展开则带有一定的实验性。但其核心仍然是riff驱动的毒草摇滚，对于偏好实验、前卫与电子声响的听众而言，距离仍较远，仅在世界音乐与实验氛围的交叉地带产生有限共鸣。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — It was no coincidence that the band's name was inspired by the work "Rainbow in Curved Air" by minimalist composer Terry Riley. Nor was it a coincidence that their third album, Phantasmagoria, was named after Lewis Carroll's longest poem. A sequence of terrifying or fantastical, dreamlike images would undoubtedly help in visualizing the album's direction.Marie Antoinette...half ballad, half rock, driven by synthesizers, Sonja's voice (who also wrote many of the songs) sways like a hammock, gradually increasing in speed until it reaches a vertigo-inducing crescendo, amplified by the bass and guitar...before the tubular bells provide the necessary pause to further highlight the rock return in the song's second part. Another piece as complex as it is beautiful, a dreamlike work with which this journey begins, a fairy tale of yesteryear...the kind reminiscent of Andersen, who didn't shy away from darkness as part of the whole, in the ideal balance of art.Melinda (More or Less), with its harpsichord and guest flute by Annie Stewart, plus Darryl Way's violin, creates a medieval atmosphere that only deepens the sense of immersion in a fiction that grows ever more real. Sonja's vocals contrast with other registers, making her contribution all the more valuable. Not Quite the Same begins with trumpets reminiscent of the Renaissance, until the jazzy drums and Sonja's syncopated vocals bring it into the present, creating another instant classic for the group.Cheetah is an instrumental where Darryl Way's violin shines in all its splendor, and the virtuosity works in favor of the dramatic and emotional tension, something that is not so frequent, doing somersaults in the air, reaching low notes among all his high notes that make it deep and dark...with the drummer and bass following in his footsteps as if it were a frantic chase.More instant classics with the title track Phantasmagoria, where the organ, violin, and drums create a floating, ethereal, and light cloud where Sonja's voice travels, carrying forward those strange melodies that made Curved Air unique, half medieval, half avant-garde...The electronic experiments return in Whose Shoulder Are You Looking Over Anyway? , which serves as an introduction to "Over and Above." After a brief respite, the trumpets, violin, and keyboards return with full force at an accelerated pace, once again recalling the symphonic passages of Renaissance, when the band was one with the orchestra. Here, however, they are enhanced by the somewhat atonal compositions of Curved Air, which left them hanging on the cliff...visible and defiant like a flag in the middle of the mountain. Frank Ricotti on xylophone is fundamental to this track, along with the trumpets and trombones, which move from jazz to classical fugues...as if it were a new symphony for the new world. The Moog solo brings a new dimension, followed by the bass, which, together with the winds and xylophone, forms an orchestra that descends into the underworld before returning to pure tubular bell and distorted electric guitar.Once a Ghost, Always a Ghost closes with a jazzy calypso rhythm, which, while shifting the dramatic tension, serves as an awakening from that dream (at times a nightmare) established from the beginning.This is the classic Curved Air from the early days, the Francis Monkman era. Eddie Jobson would later arrive to fill in for the temporary departure of its founder, Daryl Way, but that's another story. The bonus track version includes Marie Antoinette sung in French, and it's not to be missed.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑来自制作人DJ Fantôme，由世界音乐杂志Songlines进行评论。从专辑名称'Zando Beat!'推测，其音乐风格涉及非洲传统音乐（Zando为津巴布韦相关音乐类型）与电子节拍的融合，属于世界音乐与电子制作的跨界作品。DJ Fantôme以将非洲传统声响与现代电子制作相结合而闻名，在非洲独立电子场景中具有一定的独特性。该作品位于用户偏好的世界音乐与电子音乐交叉地带，但可能缺乏更深层的实验性或前卫元素。由于原文内容过短，无法对其具体编曲、声音设计及创新程度进行更深入评估。整体而言，这是一张具有一定文化特色的世界电子融合作品，但与用户最高优先级的实验/前卫/自由爵士口味存在一定距离。

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了来自78转唱片时代的印度器乐作品，涵盖北印度古典音乐、卡纳提克音乐及民间音乐传统。由音乐家、作家兼印度古典音乐收藏家罗伯特·米利斯编选，聚焦于录音史早期阶段的器乐录音，展现了印度传统音乐在录音技术萌芽时期的多样面貌。作品以历史档案式的视角呈现了萨罗德、西塔琴等多种乐器的演奏传统，具有民族音乐学的文献价值。作为世界音乐领域的资料性合辑，对关注南亚传统音乐和录音史的听众有一定吸引力，但在声音创新、实验性元素及跨类型融合方面较为有限。原文内容过短，信息量不足以全面评估其艺术价值。

items.body:
Estudiantina of Melbourne – Ta Nisia [The Islands] (self-release, 2026)

Estudiantina Of Melbourne presents its second album, Ta Nisia (The Islands), an independently-released recording. The new work follows the ensemble’s debut, Journey to Rebetika, and arrives after two years of activity that included 26 concerts.

The new album reflects both continuity and change. The group’s music remains rooted in captivating smyrneika and rebetiko, taking the listener on a tour of joyful Greek taverns and nightclubs. At the same time, Ta Nisia also points to a broader musical direction. In turn, the title carries both a literal and symbolic meaning: each track stands on its own. Nevertheless, together, the pieces trace a larger story of migration, identity, growth, and belonging.

The lineup on the album features regular ensemble members Maria Antaras-Dalamagas on accordion and vocals; Vagelis Ginis on vocals; Camille El Feghali on kanun; Jenny Dixon on violin; Alex Petropoulos on guitar; Paul Karalis on bouzouki; Con Kalamaras on bouzouki and vocals; and Rosco Heck on percussion. Guest musicians Indra Buraczewska on double bass and Tim Meyen on cimbalom also appear on the release. Meyen’s instrument, a 145-string Austro-Hungarian cimbalom, adds an unusual, charming tonal element to the ensemble’s established sound.

At the same time, Ta Nisia reflects the cultural mix of Melbourne, where the group formed and developed its identity. 

Musicians: Alex Petropoulos on guitar, vocals, lavta; Camille El Feghali on kanun, zurna; Con Kalamaras on bouzouki, vocals, lavta; Jenny Dixon on violin; Maria AntarasonDalamagas on accordion, vocals; Paul Karalis on bouzouki, oud; Rosco Heck on percussion; Vagellis Ginis on vocals. Guest musicians: Indra Buraczewska on bass; and Tim Meyen on cimbalom.

Kieran McCoey, recording engineer. Recorded at 3MBS Studios Abbotsford Convent Melbourne 2025
Album artwork by Matthew Revert.

items.body:
In this recording by bassist, composer and bandleader Ben Wolfe, titled Any Time After Now, there is a quiet assurance, with nothing straining for effect or feeling manufactured. Recorded in a single studio day alongside vibraphonist Joel Ross, pianist Sullivan Fortner, tenor saxophonist Chris Lewis and drummer Aaron Kimmel, the album spans ten tracks of original Wolfe compositions and exhibits a natural cohesion that reflects musicians deeply attuned to one another.

The opener, "Any Time After Now," swings with effortless authority. Wolfe's bass lines move with confidence beneath Lewis and Ross's contributions, while Fortner brings a strong rhythmic sense to the tune. Kimmel takes an imaginative turn on his kit, adding to the bebop narrative. "Waltz II" is striking for its delicacy. Buoyed by Wolfe's deep tone and steady beat, Ross and Fortner interact with arresting sensitivity, each phrase answered by the other.

"Blues" evokes a hazy, after-hours atmosphere. Lewis delivers an expressive performance, smoky, relaxed, and soulful. Ross follows with an improvisation rich in harmonic nuance, and Fortner settles into a blues statement grounded in groove and touch. "5/4 Groove" unfolds as Kimmel shapes the asymmetrical pulse with ease, while Fortner crafts an extended meditation brimming with momentum and tension. Wolfe's solo is a highlight, lyrical, poised, and deeply musical.

Wolfe, an unusual musician who associates music with color, shape and texture, writes compositions that carry visual weight. The music shifts between shadows, light, density and openness with remarkable fluidity. The result is a performance in which the band knows exactly how to inhabit these spaces.

"Down with Gravity" brings sharp angles and earthy funk. Wolfe and Kimmel work hand in glove, while Lewis stretches out with a harmonic vocabulary that yields clarity of ideas. There is a real bite here without sacrificing sophistication. "Always Four" opens with an assertive flourish from Kimmel, then settles into tightly focused exchanges between Ross and Fortner. Kimmel is back on board with crisp playing, taking the tune out as each idea feels purposeful.

"Til The Next Time" is a silky bossa nova that glides effortlessly into the ear. Ross, in full vibrato, phrases beautifully over Wolfe's subtle plucking. Fortner and Kimmel keep everything light and pleasant. The closing bonus track, "Green," swings with optimism and zest. Ross and Fortner carry the instrumental load with a keen sense of musical drama, while Wolfe and Kimmel deliver sharply etched pulses. The number offers a clear picture of Wolfe's melodic, thoughtful, and generous compositional voice.

Any Time After Now; Waltz II; If Only; Blues; 5/4 Groove; Do You Love?; Down with Gravity; Always Four; 'Till Next Time; Green.

items.body: Growing up in the Chicago area with Jamaican heritage running deep, Kazayah came to roots reggae as a calling. Her latest single “Mustard Seed” pairs her with Tikur Anbessa Records, the Los Angeles label run by Fikir Amlak, a singer, multi-instrumentalist and producer with 20 years in the business, and London’s King Alpha, a Ghanaian-born, West London producer and sound system operator who has spent years pressing dub and roots riddims to vinyl and taking them to sound system stages across Europe and beyond. Amlak and King Alpha have worked together since 2014, giving the record a production backbone with a decade of roots credibility behind it. The track rides a heavy steppas riddim, deep bassline and crisp percussion giving her warm, focused delivery the room to push the message forward. In both biblical and Rastafari tradition the mustard seed is faith that grows from almost nothing, and for an artist who found Rastafari as a reckoning with Black identity and cultural pride, that image runs through everything she makes, placing her in the line of Marcia Griffiths and Jah9. Stream “Mustard Seed” HERE The post Daily Discovery: Kazayah – Mustard Seed appeared first on Rhythm Passport.

items.body: The Portland, Oregon-based synth-punk duo Point Line Plane has released its self-titled debut album, “Point Line Plane,” on SKiN GRAFT Records. The release marks the first-ever vinyl pressing of the record, which was originally co-released on CD by Xeroid Records and Sincere Brutality in 2003 and has been out of print for more than twenty years. Formats include LP, CD, digital and an Ultimate Edition. The vinyl edition is pressed on 8-Bit Blue Vinyl, limited to 1500 numbered copies worldwide. Packaging includes a double-sided “Footlong” OBI with artwork by Portland designer E*Rock. A CD edition includes one bonus track not available on the LP. The Ultimate Edition adds a large-format booklet containing a memoir titled “The Future Belongs to Analog Loyalists” by guitarist Mitsuru Tabata, a comic by Rob Syers, and a pull-out poster. Point Line Plane by Point Line Plane The album was recorded and engineered by Steve Albini and Zeni Geva. Mastering of the original release was handled by Denis Blackham and Martin Bowes. Vinyl mastering for this 2026 pressing was completed in December 2025 by Carl Saff and Bob Weston. The lead single is “Death Dance 2000”, which has an official music video. About Point Line Plane Point Line Plane was formed in Portland, Oregon, around 2002 by vocalist and keyboardist Joshua Blanchard and drummer Nathan Carson as a synth-and-drums duo. Blanchard had previously performed as part of the Sensualists. Carson co-founded the Portland doom metal band Witch Mountain in 1997 and has run the booking agency Nanotear. The band’s self-titled debut was recorded and released in 2003, co-issued on CD by Xeroid Records and Sincere Brutality. That year the duo also released the single “Curse Chorus Curse / Sh…Boom” on S-S Records, contributed a cover of “Give The Future A Break” to a Screamers tribute compilation, and completed a split release with The Planet. In late 2003, Howard Gillam (also known as Supersprite) joined on second synth, expanding the lineup to a trio. As a trio, the band recorded “Smoke Signals,” released in 2004 on SKiN GRAFT Records. The band also produced the score for the feature documentary “Haunters.” Point Line Plane disbanded in 2005 after approximately 150 live performances. Both founding members continued other work. Blanchard also performs as Major Hex. Carson remained active with Witch Mountain, which has toured internationally and released records on Profound Lore Records and Svart Records. He also hosts The Heavy Metal Sewïng Cïrcle on XRAY FM, runs Nanotear Booking, and has published fiction. The original duo, Blanchard and Carson, announced their return in 2026 when SKiN GRAFT Records proposed the remastered vinyl reissue of the debut. “Point Line Plane” (SKiN GRAFT Records) is out now.

items._cn_summary: 该文章来自Peek-A-Boo暗潮/哥特杂志，介绍工业乐队Revolting Cocks（Al Jourgensen领衔的工业超级组合）翻唱Olivia Newton-John经典流行曲《Physical》的视频片段。从风格定位看，Revolting Cocks属于工业/EBM范畴，与用户偏好的暗潮工业线有直接交集。乐队本身具备一定地下工业血统，早期与Wax Trax!厂牌关联深厚。但文章内容实质上仅为视频片段展示加歌词摘录，并非原创乐评，缺乏对编曲、声响设计、演唱表现等方面的任何分析。同时，将一首1980年代流行金曲以工业手法重新演绎，虽然在工业乐迷圈层中具有一定趣味性，但整体创新空间有限。综合来看，风格匹配度尚可，但内容信息量严重不足，难以形成有价值的评价参考。

items.body:
YOUTH return with a second dose of inexorable House pressure from Paul Bennett aka Duster Valentine, primed for DJs and dancers and a sureshot tip FFO Michael J. Blood, Todd Terry, Ron Trent, Anthony “Shake” Shakir, DJ Sprinkles…

Aye it’s another haul of hard hitting gems pressed to vinyl for the first time, a love note to formative years in the ‘80s and early ‘90s, off his chops at The Haçienda and other legendary Manchester spots. It’s a masterclass in demonstrating the flavours-within-a-theme that emerged from the Chi, 313, and NYC during that pivotal era, and which would eventually light the touch paper of a UK club revolution. 

In Duster Valentine’s hands, the sound is presented stripped to salient fundamentals, before it went commercial, ranging from sampler-knuckling garage-house stabbers thru haughty canter and plushest, pendulous grooves. He homes in hard on the exact point when hip hop and electro gave way to house in the Todd Terry-via-Pal Joey style jam ‘Getting’ Dub’, and gives a big salute to Chez N Trent’s rugged, chord-riding haughtiness via Levon Vincent in ‘Hit Me From Behind’.

‘Strobelight Honnies’ leans into the sound’s deepest ends with a perfectly weighted bassline, cold drums and sublime string tension dubbed with hypnotic elegance, where ‘The KatG Chord’ follows with shimmers of Anthony Shakir via Michael J Blood. Suffice it to say they’re all essential and bang on the dollar if you know what’s good.

100% perlers!
items._cn_summary: 这是Duster Valentine（Paul Bennett）的House音乐专辑，风格根植于上世纪八九十年代芝加哥、底特律和纽约的House传统。乐评将其与Michael J. Blood、Todd Terry、Ron Trent、Anthony Shakir、DJ Sprinkles等艺术家并列，描述为对早期俱乐部场景的致敬。专辑涵盖车库House切分节拍、沉稳的低音线条和催眠式弦乐张力，强调对经典House元素的精确还原与呈现。制作注重节奏与律动的扎实感，风格偏向舞池实用主义，虽具有电子音乐的底色，但更接近传统Deep House的范畴，与实验电子、IDM、氛围或暗潮等领域的距离较远。

items.body:
A strong breeze of Cajun twang from 1920’s Louisiana, delivered by the excellent Death Is Not The End 

Taking its title from the first in a series of Cajun recordings made in New Orleans and released by Columbia Records, namely the Segura Brothers’ Bury Me In The Corner Of The Yard, the rest of the set follows suit with infectious stompers, rattlers and wheezers about whiskey-running, unrequited love and turtle stew, by excellent names such as Artelus Mistric and Blind Uncle Gaspard, all with equally charming tunes to boot.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张由Death Is Not The End厂牌策划的1920年代路易斯安那州卡津音乐合集，原始录音由哥伦比亚唱片发行。合辑收录了Artelus Mistric、Blind Uncle Gaspard等艺人的早期卡津作品，内容涉及私酒贩运、单恋和龟肉汤等生活主题，音乐风格为带有手风琴和小提琴的传统卡津民谣，节奏明快粗犷。Death Is Not The End作为专注于挖掘冷门档案录音的独立厂牌，为这些老录音赋予了一定的地下策展视角，但其本质仍为传统民间音乐，与实验、前卫或融合类音乐距离较远。作为美国本土根源音乐的一种，它在世界音乐范畴内有一定价值，但缺乏与用户偏好的电子、爵士或实验元素的交集，整体定位偏向档案性质的民谣再版。

items.body: Review by Hector Enrique — Far from settling for the melodic formulas that defined much of the neo-prog of the 1980s and 1990s -and which they themselves had masterfully embodied- Pendragon took a bold turn towards rougher, more aggressive sounds -without, of course, losing sight of their sensitive DNA- with the daring "Believe" (2005). Three years later, they confirmed this evolution with the darker, more intense and instrumentally forceful "Pure" (2008), their eighth studio album.The muscular, overdriven guitar opening of the lengthy "Indigo" -arguably the album's finest track-, dramatised by distant dog barks, the psychedelia of its middle section built upon Clive Nolan's keyboards and Nick Barrett's two lengthy, enveloping solos -clearly Gilmourian in style- reflect the rockier path Pendragon chose to tread during the 2000s. A direction which, whilst keeping their neo-prog roots intact, introduces harder-edged riffs and magnetic atmospheres that bring the band closer to heavy prog territory, without quite reaching an industrial aesthetic, as can be heard in the furious "Eraserhead", the contemplative "Comatose I: View from the Seashore" or the energetic "The Freak Show".In a conceptual work that conveys a constant sense of unease, introspection and personal quest -epitomised by a troubled young contortionist unable to find meaning in his existence- the funkier and, at times, spacey "Comatose II: Space Cadet" and the mesmerising "Comatose III: Home and Dry" bring back the band's more melodic and crystalline side. Finally, the emotive arpeggiated ballad "It's Only Me", which drags on in its development, fails to blend naturally into the whole, partially blurring the concluding section of "Pure", an album that represented one of the rawest and most oppressive journeys in Pendragon's career.3.5 stars
items._cn_summary: Pendragon 2008年专辑《Pure》属于新前卫摇滚（Neo-Prog）范畴，延续了乐队自《Believe》以来向更粗粝、更具侵略性方向转型的路线。专辑以过载吉他开场，融入迷幻段落、键盘音色和较长的吉他独奏，在新前卫摇滚根基上引入了更硬朗的riff和沉重的氛围，接近重金属前卫的领域但未完全进入工业风格。概念上围绕一个困惑的年轻柔术演员展开，主题涉及不安、内省与个人追寻。部分曲目带有放克和太空感元素，展现了旋律性与力量感的交替。整体制作保持了较强的可听性，以吉他为主导的摇滚编曲为主，实验性和电子元素较少，与前卫实验、工业电子等方向存在一定距离。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — One of the most traditional flamenco sounding Spanish bands of the Rock Andaluz scene that tookSpain by storm in the late 70s and early 80s, the rather ridiculously named CAL that put out oneself-titled album with a rather bland and uninspiring album cover emerged from Seville's fertileflamenco rock scene following in the footsteps of Triana, Alameda and other predecessors. The lineupfeatured keyboardist and vocalist Alberto Toribio who was one of the pioneers of the style in theband Goma. Also along for the ride were Pepe Fern�ndez (guitar, vocals), Francisco Mu�oz (bass,vocals) and Juanjo Mu�oz (drums, vocals). Like many of the flamenco prog bands of the era, CAL (ironically there was another band at the timenamed Cai) took the world of flamenco and applied it to the context of symphonic prog but unlike thevibrant complexities of bands like Mezquita, Triana, Guadalquivir or Azahar, this band was mostlysteeped in its flamenco roots with the symphonic prog aspects providing a less dominant rolealthough the band made use of its share of mellotron, synthesizers and pianos with some moments ofnon-flamenco prog emerging along with the acoustic guitar, handclaps and castanets. Generallyspeaking the prog aspects are primarily used for intros and interludes while the flamenco partydominates the majority of the song structures.This album featured seven tracks running at about 35 minutes and primarily features rather simplecompositions that seem lazy and uninspired as much so as the rather ridiculous album cover art. Infact the whole thing feels like a frantic cash in while the Rock Andaluz boom was still hot. Whilethe music is a touch jazzier than most with fusion-like keyboards finding their way into the mix andsome extended song structures that qualify the album as bonafide progressive rock mostly in thelatter third of the album with tracks like "Ensayo En El Garbanzo" and the near 10-minute two-partcloser "Colgao" finally delivering the goods, overall it's a fairly insipidly weak affair with thatvibe of just barely getting the job done.No doubt about it, CAL was one of the weaker acts of the entire Rock Andaluz scene yet despite theband not really standing out in any particular way or sounding like what you would think eitherTriana or Alameda would sound like in demo form, the music isn't offensively banal or unlistenablein any way however in this fertile passionate micro-nook of the prog universe it just seems ratherbland and uninspiring and rather unessential in relation to some of the excellent bands that existedat the same time and considering that this band came from Seville, the Mecca of all things flamencoand cross-pollinating extensions, it sounds even less captivating! There isn't really anything ilike about this one. The band name is meh, the album cover is blah, the performances are mediocreand the compositors are ugh however it's still a good album as it delivers just enough spice to keepit from coming off as watered down gazpacho and even weak flamenco rock is still endearing to acertain degree.
items._cn_summary: 这张1980年的西班牙专辑来自Rock Andaluz乐潮，融合弗拉门戈与交响前卫摇滚。乐队来自塞维利亚，以键盘手Alberto Toribio为核心，编制包括吉他、贝斯与鼓。乐评整体评价偏低，指出该作在弗拉门戈根基上嫁接交响前卫元素，但前卫部分仅在引子和间奏出现，主体仍以传统弗拉门戈节奏与吉他为主，合成器与钢琴运用保守。专辑共七首曲目约35分钟，作曲被指简单且缺乏灵感，仅在末尾的《Ensayo En El Garbanzo》和近十分钟的《Colgao》中展现了较为完整的渐进式结构。乐评将其归为Rock Andaluz场景中较弱的乐队之一，认为其缺乏Triana或Alameda的辨识度与感染力，整体平庸。

items.body: Review by KansasForEver4 — A band with a Tennessee vibe? Well, yes, because EVERSHIP hails from Nashville, a city better known for rock 'n' roll and bananas than for progressive rock! Yet it's from there that Shane Atkinson decided to send us his flagship album. Shane is a multi-instrumentalist composer who worked as a studio musician in the eighties and nineties, even composing commercials and film scores to make ends meet. After dabbling in the software industry, music haunted him so much that he decided to return to it, starting in 2005 with his own recording studio and equipment. The first compositions for the album presented here date back to 2009, so seven solid years to arrive at the remarkable result of this self-titled debut album.hane Atkinson handled almost all the instruments, with a few guest musicians including his own brother James on acoustic and lead guitars, and the invaluable vocal contribution of Beau West, an old childhood friend. And what vocals they are! From the very first track, "Silver Light," Freddie must be turning in his grave, so strongly does the song's emphasis evoke Queen, so powerfully operatic?an influence claimed (among others) by the master of ceremonies himself, the Queen of the pre-"News of the World" era, the very rock, frenetic Queen of the first five albums. The second track, "A Slow Descent Into Reality," takes us back to Liverpool in 1970 (and even earlier?), so strong is the influence of the Merseyside quartet in the opening. This is further enhanced by Queen's operatic feel, a touch of Kansas from Nicelle Priebe's violin, and a dash of classic Yes (the intricate bass lines and enchanting backing vocals). In short, a veritable who's who of the genre, all showcased by Shane Atkinson's multifaceted talent.And what can be said about the splendid "Evermore" that follows? Calm, delicate, and melodic (both divine and lyrical), with a magical piano, the electric guitar takes on a Bostonian character (though recapturing Tom Scholz's distinctive sound is no easy feat), and, as always, those majestic and magnificent backing vocals?a truly great moment of progressive rock. "Ultima Thule" continues in the same vein, a clear vocal tribute to our dearly departed Freddie and Brad in particular. Beau West establishes himself as an undeniable heir with his shimmering and delicate timbre, all sprinkled with a sublime violin in the finale. It's beautiful, it's wonderful...We thought we'd heard it all, but no! "Flying Machine" nails us to the delightful pillory of timeless progressive music. Our bliss and delight are unparalleled. The choirs, always the choirs (again, Boston, and also the entire musical spectrum of melodic rock from the last thirty years, not forgetting, on the other side of the Atlantic, the ever-popular Moody Blues), flood this track from beginning to end, and the orchestrations are simply fabulous.One minor point, but one that only concerns your reviewer: I didn't recognize the Theremin and Dulcimer that are supposed to be on the album. And a small criticism of this work: there's a lot of singing, but it's so well sung that forgiveness is in order.Another contender for the podium, a podium for which three steps won't be enough this year.Simply magnificent.Thank you, Mr. Atkinson.
items._cn_summary: 纳什维尔乐队EVERSHIP的首张同名专辑定位为新前卫摇滚，核心创作人Shane Atkinson几乎包揽所有乐器演奏，邀请主唱Beau West献声。整张专辑深受七十年代经典乐队影响，Queen的华丽歌剧摇滚、披头士的旋律质感、Yes的复杂贝斯线条、Boston的合唱编排以及Moody Blues的氛围营造均清晰可辨。编曲以宏大合唱、壮丽管弦乐和细腻钢琴为主导，技术扎实，旋律流畅。虽属前卫摇滚类别，但作品整体趋向对经典摇滚传统的致敬与复刻，在声响实验、跨界融合及原创性方面表现有限，更接近传统新前卫摇滚的怀旧路线。

items.body: Norwegian solo artist Chris Wicked releases a gothic rock and dark synthpop cover of Depeche Mode‘s “Enjoy the Silence” on June 2, 2026, via Raven Black Productions. The Bergen-based artist here mixes gothic, cinematic and alternative rock. This is the third single from his forthcoming EP “Black Horns & Black Hooves.” Chris Wicked explains his reasons for choosing the song: “Enjoy the Silence has always been a song that resonated with me. The atmosphere, the sense of longing and the timeless darkness within the melody have inspired me since I was young. We didn’t want to copy the original — we wanted to reinterpret it through our own musical universe.” The cover arrives as the third single from the upcoming EP “Black Horns & Black Hooves” on Raven Black Productions. It follows “Utan Dina Andetag,” a cover of a Kent track released in December 2024 as the first single from the project, and “Wicked Game,” a cover of the Chris Isaak song released in September 2025 as the second single. About Chris Wicked Chris Wicked is a solo artist from Bergen, Norway. He came to wider attention as the founder and vocalist of Malice In Wonderland, a Norwegian rock band formed in the late 1990s before releasing a debut album and single “Lucifer’s Town” in 2005. Musically Malice In Wonderland’s sound combines glam, goth and hard rock elements. The band toured across Europe and Asia, sharing stages with acts including Def Leppard, and appeared in television productions. Their final album, “The Royal Brigade,” was released in December 2013, mixed by John Fryer, known for his work with Depeche Mode and Nine Inch Nails. In August 2015, Malice In Wonderland announced their break-up and completed a series of farewell shows in Norway and abroad. Chris Wicked subsequently announced a solo career, recording under his own name. His debut solo album, “Aleine,” was released in 2021 via Apollon Records and featured guest appearances from Gaahl (Gorgoroth), Hoest (Taake), Niklas Kvarforth (Shining) and V’gandr (Helheim). In 2024, he released the dark Nordic folk single “Northern Heart” on Raven Black Productions. Malice In Wonderland returned in 2025 to mark the 20th anniversary of their 2005 debut, releasing new and reimagined material including “I’ve Chosen Darkness (Over You)” and a revisited edition of “Lucifer’s Town” in 2025, followed by the single “Dying Breed” in 2026.

items.body:
Storybook: The Music Of Mark Miller is at one level the unfolding narrative of its 10 musical selections. At another, it is a tale about its primary author, Mark Miller, who traced his journey from {jny: Racine}} to New York City with his previous release Mark Miller: The Return Of Slide Huxtable (Slide Huxtable, 2008)—a long road that is a serious jazz player's dream of making it in the Big Apple. But most of all, it is a compelling reminder to listeners everywhere that the Manhattan jazz experience is incomplete without a trip to hear the Birdland Big Band.

Birdland's original, long defunct basement club at "The Jazz Corner of the World" (Broadway and 52nd) now occupies a bigger mid-town area, bounded on the north by Jazz at Lincoln Center (60 St.) and, on the south, by the "new" Birdland (44th St). Start at 52nd St., walk 8 blocks in either direction, and you are there. But which direction? Is there a significant difference? Some observers have suggested that big band music from the north references the genius of Duke Ellington, whereas the sounds to the south are aligned with the swing of Count Basie. Yet "Storybook," the eponymous title of the album's Grammy-nominated first track, sounds like something else entirely.

Miller—much of whose "schooling" was on the road as trombonist-composer with the Minneapolis-based jazz group, The Motion Poets—has constructed a brilliant sonic gateway that owes as much to Bach and Bartok as to Ellington or Count Basie. Starting with a stately 3-note descending motif, the composition builds on that figure with rich harmonies and vibrant dynamics, answered by an ascending counter-melody played by the lower brass. Soon, the entire sequence is repeated, with the addition of creative commentary from Brandon Lee's flugelhorn. After a sharply articulated, vigorously syncopated version of the primary motif, Kenny Barron's infectious "Water Lily." Unlike earlier recorded versions that are slower and light-spirited, the tune here is taken at a driving tempo with accompaniment by piano and drums that borders on the intrusive (likely due to an over-hot audio mix-down). Besides an inventive piano solo by Kenny Ascher, the piece showcases the commanding artistry of saxophonist Troy Roberts, whose closing cadenza balances impressive pyrotechnics with satisfying musical taste. Next, the standard, "Tenderly," lightens the mood with a sprightly version of a waltz that, with the notable exception of Bill Evans' up-tempo version, usually receives the slow, pensive reading of Rosemary Clooney or the even slower 4/4 versions by Sara Vaughn and Billie Holiday. Miller's arrangement exhibits remarkable attention to detail, replete with spiraling flutes that simulate butterflies to complement the spring setting for vocalist Nicole Zuraitis. Brief solos by Sam Dillon (a. sax) and Raul Agraz (trpt) fit seamlessly with the colorful seasonal mix.

Miller's own "Chorale and Alleluia" is as contemplative and celebratory as its title might suggest. It features the percussive thunder of Chris Smith, who will also be critical to the driving samba rhythm of Chick Corea's "Spain." Tom Harrell's "Sail Away" is an inviting melody launched without affectation by Glenn Drewes' reassuring flugel. After band director David DeJesus' soprano sax has taken control of the cruise, Drews resumes his storytelling by, in effect, shutting off the engine (i.e., piano, bass, drums) and allowing only the sounds of wind and water for several choruses—the pulse of the band sans rhythm section.

It is tempting to continue with a play-by-play analysis if only to identify the soloists in an ensemble with no weak links. The Birdland Band is "deep" with talent, each player capable of assuming solo duties on any given night. Take, for example, "WTF," in which trombonist/composer Miller resumes the cruise with a witty trombone exchange between James Burton III and Sara Jacovino, one that recalls the musical conversations by J.J. Johnson and Jay and Kai Winding.

The last third of the program is cued up by the standard "Close Your Eyes," which opens with Zuraitis close to the mic as she fashions a soft, pitch-perfect, improvised chorus before yielding to an Ascher piano solo that swings with the sure-fingered authority of Wynton Kelly. Following a good-humored, equally swinging turn by bass trombonist, James Borowski, Zuraitis re-enters for an "out" chorus that soon becomes "far-out," her voice rising in pitch and volume to the level of a Maynard Ferguson set-closer. It works because the vocalist implants herself in the trumpet section, rising to a powerful climax as the job requires. Finally, we receive a healthy reminder that "swing" does not require a thing except a ride cymbal and a hi-hat. (If only audio engineers could figure out a way to include the shimmer of a Zildjian in their mastering of live sounds.)

Rodrigo de Arunez's "Concierto" and Corea's "Spain" are worthy additions to those already in print. And they are among the most "honest," avoiding orchestral instruments (French horns, double reeds, tympani, etc.) as well as electronic devices (Fender Rhodes, phaser boxes, onboard modulating effects). The result is a focus that remains fixed on the music, not the gear. And then there is the memorable close-out for "Spain"—an ascending Miller bass-line that, in effect, resolves a sparking, fractious debate between big band and drums, then between sections within the ensemble.

"The DoubleDown," the last track of the regular program, evokes a Sunday night gospel meeting with its inviting singalong melody in ¾. The primary preacher is Ron Wilkins, whose testifying on plunger-muted trombone produces a meditative bass solo by Noriko Ueda. But rather than exit quietly, the congregation is led back by saxophones to the main theme, then a sudden stop and lift to a new key for a final testament by Mark Miller's emphatic postlude on trombone.

Church is out, but the congregation's spirits crave more action. "Nonsense," an original shuffle-rhythm blues composed by Miller and Zuraitis, answers the need to sustain the sense of play embedded in every true storybook. Zuraitis delivers a nonsensical lyric in the strongest musical terms, conversing over stop-time chords with Miller's and Wilkins' vocal trombones. Next, she handles "vocalese" lines in tight unison with tricky instrumental figures. Finally, there is a vocal exchange, over pedal-tone bass, between the entire band and its girl singer, who has the last word: "Nonsense? Come on, whatever gets you.

Small wonder that, after hearing a call like that, visitors are setting aside Friday nights for a return to Birdland.

items.body: Russian punk collective Pussy Riot announced “CYKA,” their debut full-length album, scheduled for release on June 12, 2026, on digital streaming platforms. The fourteen-track record compresses fourteen years of the group’s activity – including protest actions, imprisonment and exile – into a single body of work. The album title translates from Russian as “bitch.” Lead single “Candy Dopamine,” featuring Avenged Sevenfold, is out now with an official music video on YouTube. “Candy Dopamine” was co-written by Pussy Riot with Avenged Sevenfold vocalist M. Shadows and guitarist Zacky Vengeance. The track mixes pop with alternative rock and features guest vocals from M. Shadows alongside heavy guitar work. Pussy Riot founder Nadya Tolokonnikova described the song as a statement on prescription and designer drug culture: “It started with my dependence on antidepressants, but it’s also looking at everyone now, mentalhealthmaxxing and looksmaxxing via pills and injections. It’s not a judgment, it’s just an observation, and my personal experience with these things is that I have to be in a long-term relationship with them for my PTSD and depression.” This is the second collaboration between Avenged Sevenfold and Pussy Riot. In 2023, Tolokonnikova appeared on a reworked version of the Avenged Sevenfold track “We Love You,” re-released as “We Love You Moar,” raising awareness of the situation of LGBTQ+ people in Russia. The album’s earlier single “Disobey” was released in May 2026. Its music video consists of footage from Pussy Riot’s “Storm of Venice” protest action at the 61st Venice Biennale, in which more than fifty members of the collective stormed the Russian pavilion with clouds of pink smoke. Ukrainian activist group FEMEN joined the demonstration, which was staged in protest at Russia’s return to the international art event. The 90-second track features distorted guitars, shouted vocals and chants of “disobey,” with lyrics in English and Russian condemning fascism and political silence. ‘CYKA’: collaborators, tracklist, and Putin challenge Other confirmed contributors on “CYKA” include B-Real of Cypress Hill (on the track “Gore”) and singer-songwriter Salem Ilese (on “Utopia”). Russian President Vladimir Putin is listed as a contributor on the self-titled track “Cyka.” Tolokonnikova adds: “I’m not gonna give him royalties though, they can add it to my list of crimes.” Tolokonnikova also announced a public challenge to Putin to fight her at the UFC Freedom 250 event, scheduled for June 14 at the White House. In her statement, she says: “All these old men ruining the world right now act tough, but we see through their fragile egos, and I’m not afraid to call them out. I challenge President Putin to a cage match. He loses? He gets the fuck out of Ukraine.” About Pussy Riot Pussy Riot is a Russian punk and protest collective founded in Moscow in 2011. The group operates as a loose, rotating collective but is closely associated with founders Nadya Tolokonnikova (also known as Nadya Tolokno) and Maria Alyokhina (known as Masha). The group staged performances in public spaces across Moscow as acts of political protest, often wearing brightly colored balaclavas. In February 2012, three members – Tolokonnikova, Alyokhina and Yekaterina Samutsevich – were arrested following a performance inside Moscow’s Cathedral of Christ the Saviour. They were convicted of “hooliganism motivated by religious hatred” and sentenced to two years in a penal colony. Samutsevich was released on appeal in October 2012; Tolokonnikova and Alyokhina served their full sentences, released in December 2013. The trial attracted international attention. Following their release, Tolokonnikova and Alyokhina continued their political activism and released music under the Pussy Riot name. The group collaborated with Boys Noize on “Rage” in 2021, and with Boyfriend on the electropop single “Dance With the Devil” in 2023. In July 2025, a new Russian law criminalized searching for Pussy Riot content online. In April 2026, Tolokonnikova was formally indicted by Russia’s Investigative Committee for alleged violations of the country’s “foreign agent” law. “CYKA” is Pussy Riot’s debut full-length album. It is released June 12, 2026.

items.body:
A House Of My Own by Mark Grusane via Disctechno.

"Mark Grusane's latest offering, A House of My Own is a testament to his long-standing discipleship to the craft of producing hard-hitting house tracks with authenticity and depth.

The title-bearing opener on A1 strongly demonstrates this notion with a slew of raw bass stabs and emotive pads leading through a battery of driven percussion in a manner that calls to mind those early 90's Mr. Fingers records. While A2's Essence of Life (Afterhours Mix) takes us further into the darkness with a spiraling timber of percussions lain over distorted vocal arrangements, the "Daytime Mix" of A3 builds on the momentum of its predecessor with a robust uplifting synth lead and sounds of atmospheric ambiance added to the mixture, effectively taking the composition to an entirely new level.

B1 kicks off punching and swinging with the track Knock knock, Who's there?, a ferocious gut-puncher of a track that sees classic Chicago "beat-track" style 909 arrangements lay over an intense saturated 303 bassline that relentlessly worms its way throughout the mix with a booming urgency. B2 sees a turn for the naughty on the track Love And Lust with a xxx-rated vocal line slithering its way through the track, sandwiched in between high-pitched keys and a slinky drumline. Finally, Jack Your Ass Off closes out the album and ties it all together on B3 showcasing the full-fledged insanity of the classic trademark Chicago "jack" style that sees the title of the track frantically screamed over and over though a sampler amid hard hitting drums and 303s engineered to make you dance like a freak."
items._cn_summary: Mark Grusane 的专辑《A House Of My Own》是一张扎根于九十年代初期芝加哥浩室传统的作品，以经典的 909 鼓机和 303 贝斯线为核心，辅以粗犷的低频刺音、情感化的合成器铺垫和传统 jack 风格的节奏律动。整张专辑呈现出对芝加哥浩室黄金年代的致敬姿态，从 Mr. Fingers 式的深情氛围到 B1 的强劲芝加哥 beat-track 风格，再到 B3 的疯狂 jack 收尾，均显示出作者对传统制作语汇的熟稔。然而该作品在类型上属于较为传统和怀旧的浩室舞曲，与听众偏好的实验电子、IDM、氛围及先锋类电子方向存在明显距离，缺少跨类型融合或声音设计层面的突破。Disctechno 厂牌虽属独立范畴，但作品本身更偏向类型内部的致敬而非创新，整体定位偏向舞曲场景而非实验聆听。

items.body:
Wino finally drop the long-teased label debut of Dublin pal Officer John, operating with a sort of dusted trip hop energy that starts off full of baggy swagger and gets more blissed as we go, finishing off with a remix from long serving label captain Morgan Buckley. 

Wino cap off an imperial 2025 with a 6 track peach from Niall Rogers aka Officer John, opening with sleeper hit ‘Stay’ that comes like The Beta Band riffing on MBV’s ‘soon’, before ‘Pass’ takes us to a more downbeat landscape just north of A.S.O., while ‘Handle’ feels like a late summer afternoon soundtracked by some Escho ace. To end, Morgan Buckley ups the funky drummer and stutters the vox for a classic slice of 90’s balearic-pop.

It’s all so naggingly ear-wormy and achingly familiar that it already feels like a classic. Sleep and, um, weep?!
items._cn_summary: 这是爱尔兰都柏林音乐人 Officer John（Niall Rogers）在独立厂牌 Wino 发行的一张六首曲目专辑，融合了 trip hop、downtempo 电子乐、baggy indie 和九十年代 balearic pop 等元素。乐评将其开场曲与 The Beta Band 改编 MBV 的风格相类比，整体氛围被描述为松散、迷幻、带 lo-fi 颗粒感的电子声响，结尾附有厂牌主理人 Morgan Buckley 的混音作品。音乐风格偏向可听性较强的独立电子和梦幻流行，并未涉及实验性声响设计、IDM、ambient、glitch 或前卫爵士等领域。整体定位为小厂牌独立电子小品，风格亲切熟悉但创新性有限。

items.body:
Slowe – In Moments (Tru Thoughts TRU480D, 2026)

Slowe’s In Moments glows with intimate and hard-earned clarity. The Bristol (UK) artist deepens the neo-soul and accessible jazz palette of her earlier work, Where The Mind Wanders, with fuller arrangements and rich instrumentation. The song “How Hard Can It Be?” sways with smoky confidence, while “Sundown” drifts through quiet resilience. “Puzzle” and “Mind/Body” linger like streetlights through rain-streaked windows. Elsewhere, “Pen to Paper” and “Rhyme or Reason” strip everything bare, exposing thoughts that feel almost too delicate to voice aloud.

Slowe writes about adulthood with serenity. Anxiety, shifting relationships and the strange ache of self-awareness are conveyed in small, precise observations that cut deep. Her silky, lovely, delightful voice holds remarkable emotional gravity. 

What stays long after the final track fades is the album’s compassionate honesty. In Moments understands that change rarely arrives with triumph. More often, it slips quietly into ordinary days, leaving people startled by who they have become. Slowe captures that truth with rare elegance and radiant restraint.

Slowe shared: “This album is a meditation on change: fearing it, needing it and learning to let it shape me. Across its songs run the threads of self-doubt, shifting relationships, quiet joys and the bittersweet weight of time. It’s about the laughter that erupts without reason, the sting of tears in the middle of happiness, the moments when the heart takes a step before the mind is ready.”

Buy In Moments.

Author: Madison Quinn

items._cn_summary: 英国布里斯托艺人Slowe的专辑《In Moments》以新灵魂乐与易接受爵士（accessible jazz）为核心，编曲饱满，乐器编制丰富。整体风格偏向精致流畅的主流爵士人声路线，旋律舒缓，歌词聚焦于成年的焦虑、关系变迁与自我认知等主题，情感表达细腻但不具实验性或前卫性。制作精良，人声被描述为丝滑优雅，但声响设计保守，缺乏即兴自由爵士、电子元素或非常规结构的探索。对于偏好实验前卫、自由即兴、电子与暗潮的听众而言，该作与个人审美距离较远，属于高品质但风格安全的传统爵士人声范畴。

items.body: Review by uribreitman — An incredibly underrated blast from the not-so-distant past of (almost totally) instrumental prog. I would consider it a lost (almost lyrics-less) RUSH album from the late 70s, indeed.It has absolutely great trio-work, very similar to hard-prog outfits from the golden age.I love the fact that it doesn't follow any past convention, and just does whatever it wants.The most unique feature of the album (can't name it here, it's sooo long) that it isn't completely instrumental: The 11th track, "Halation", has some kind of sch-fi narration, which is very surprising but also highly evocative. Then it slides back to instrumental mode, like a theatrical finale closing, which is just what this album needs.To sum up this secret project, "Transmutations..." will appeal to RUSH fans which seek some mysterious and enigmatic music in their lives, while still hard-rocky and reflective. I find the lack of lyrics comforting and flat-out enjoyable. It's a shame that Maximum Indifference's (Mark, Rich and Gustaf) work met with, well - max global indifference. Recently I've found the album streaming safely on YouTube, so it's not totally gone.Give it a shot, and it'll grow on you like the old classics. I won't lie: It doesn't have the Neil Peart wise insights about the world, but it has plenty of melodic hooks, right-on riffs and brilliant ensemble playing. Clearly not essential listening, but excellent nonetheless.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张2000年发行的跨界前卫摇滚专辑，由三人组合演奏，以器乐为主。整体风格偏向七十年代末的硬式前卫摇滚，带有Rush式的技术性合奏与摇滚能量。专辑最大特色在于几乎不依赖人声，仅在第十一首"Halation"中加入了科幻风格的口述旁白，随后又回归器乐模式，形成戏剧性的收尾。编曲注重旋律钩子、强劲riff和整体合奏的平衡。作为一张被严重低估的独立小厂牌作品，它在主流前卫摇滚框架内展现了自由不拘的创作态度，但对追求实验性、爵士即兴或电子声响的听众而言，其风格仍偏向传统硬摇滚与经典前卫摇滚的范畴，缺乏更深层的跨界融合。

items.body: Review by alainPP — 35 Tapes, sounds of the 70s, Genesis, Camel, and King Crimson. The studio band uses the 35 tapes as a reference point in the Mellotron, combining them with symphonic neo-prog."Hallway" is vintage pop-rock on period keyboards, hinting at the Crimson sound with its ethereal guitars. The rapid variation on the wooden piano evokes a solemn memory, the marshmallow guitar amplifying the meditative, nostalgic atmosphere. "Water" features languid Crimson-esque keyboards, Hackett-like guitar, a somber, melancholic air with hushed vocals, and a prominent bass reminiscent of Genesis's second era. The melting pot transforms into a musical axolotl, suspended between two worlds, with a melancholic finale. "Brise" combines soft keyboards and languid, contemplative vocal harmonies. The sound recalls Rick Miller's work with Hackett-style guitar, focusing on his psychic self etched in the mirror. A fusion of delicate, ever-evolving pop-rock sounds, a melancholic instrumental drift?the key word for this album. An ethereal, Genesis-esque, nostalgic, radiant finale."Borrowed Time" features a prominent bassline of symphonic prog rock, tearful and emotionally charged. The distant acoustic Greek guitar melody evokes the intense, charismatic atmosphere of Genesis, a magnified ersatz. A plaintive final guitar solo melts the listener's heart. "Clueless" is pop-rock with a rich vocal and a catchy, yet not over-the-top, rhythm. A touch of Canterbury lends itself to this meandering, timeless journey, allowing you to savor this vintage, cinematic moment. "Cities" opens with a melting, marshmallow-like guitar solo, a nostalgic beauty. The compressed melancholy recalls the aura of King Crimson, with vocals reminiscent of John. A shimmering piece poised between sadness and hope, the mystery of its composition blends numerous references to the 70s. The contained explosion, bass and organ intertwined for the keyboard finale on "Burning Rope," is fresh and joyful, filling the atmosphere with its energy.35 Tapes offers an immersion into misty realms where reality and imagination merge. Expect introspection, Mellotron, emotion, gentleness, and warmth.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张以七十年代复古风格为核心的交响前卫摇滚专辑，大量使用Mellotron和时代键盘音色，创作灵感明显源自Genesis、Camel、King Crimson等经典乐队。整体氛围忧郁沉思，融合了Canterbury的散漫气质与流行摇滚的旋律感。编曲注重键盘与吉他的对话，段落编排工整但缺乏突破性创新，呈现出高度致敬经典的怀旧气质。作品在情绪营造上偏向柔和温暖，以追忆和内省为关键词，适合偏好传统前卫摇滚的听众，与实验性、跨界融合的审美取向存在较大距离。

items.body: Review by The Progolyte — With members from bands I've already reviewed (Raccomandata Ricevuta Ritorno, Teoremi, and L'Uovo Di Colombo), Samadhi worked similarly to Il Volo, being a supergroup that leaned to the more pop aspects of Rock Progressivo Italiano. At only thirty five minutes long, I can definitely see room for improvement, but overall, a fine record that captures that more charming aspects of Italian prog at the time. It has a symphonic twinge that works well with the nature of the group, and though it can feel a little lackluster or uninspired, I can see a strong vision that came out as an okay project. The front cover also could've been more interesting other than just the simplistic design it holds. Moving on, among the players of the band, I overall enjoyed Luciano Regoli's vocals the most, as they fit the warm atmosphere of the music. The majority of the songs are all quite short, only being a few minutes long, but each of them has a nice whimsy to it that fills the area with a fun spirit. One thing I thought could've had more work was the production, as it feels a too hazy and it can come off as a little weak at points. My favorites from this album were the joyous and energized opener of Uomo Stanco, the quirky and sweet sound of L'Angelo, the cooler jam band vibes of Passaggio Di Via Arpino, and the longer more classically influenced L'Ultima Spiaggia, which also closes the record. On this album I could hear elements of what would later form into the sound of Maxophone, having that playful yet secretly quite intricate sound. On here, however, it can come off as feeling pretentious or that the band thinks they're doing something much more grand and greater than it actually is. Sure, it's good music with some pretty good high points here and there, but I wouldn't say it's life changing or anything. In conclusion, Samadhi is essentially just your run-of-the-mill Rock Progressivo Italiano record. Nothing mind-blowing, just some good tunes with some fine details sprinkled in. I'm thinking a strong 3.25/5 or a light 3.5/5 for this one.

Feel the rush of music and be engulfed by the spectral soundscape created by the all-star lineup of the iHeartRadio Music Festival 2026. Featuring some of music's greatest talents, the two-day festival, taking place on 18 and 19 September at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, is set to be a celebration of culture, artistry, and fun.

 
 
 
 
 
View this post on Instagram
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

A post shared by iHeartRadio (@iheartradio)

The stacked roster features some era-defining names alongside rising stars who have been owning the charts as of late. Representing Asia on a global stage once more and reinforcing their legendary status as one of the greatest K-pop boy bands of all time is BTS. As they 'SWIM' through the overwhelming waves of success created by their comeback album ARIRANG, they return to festival stages once more.

Performing on night one, they are ready to deliver the same fiery passion and swagger that has defined their journey as one of the world's most notable K-pop idols. As of now, BTS are the only Asian artists featured on the list of artists performing, with more names set to be announced. The South Korean heavyweights claim their spot on the roster among some of the most legendary Western artists of all time.

IT’S OFFICIAL! BTS IS PERFORMING ON OUR STAGE THIS SEPTEMBER!

💜💜💜💜💜💜💜@BTS_twt @bts_bighit

More #iHeartFestival info: https://t.co/4lzimzHcfk pic.twitter.com/VAjlun6NzU

— iHeartRadio (@iHeartRadio) June 2, 2026

Also featured on the lineup for night one are the Goo Goo Dolls, with their soaring alternative rock and pop-infused melodies that bring a tidal wave of nostalgia with each verse. Keeping the energy high, Weezer switches up the vibes with a vast discography that spans pop-punk and rock-tinged rhythms. Adding another layer to the genre-blurring lineup is Cardi B, who is set to serve up top-tier rap verses and unbeatable lyricism as she spits some of her greatest hits on stage.

Get ready to sing every word with the crowd when @Weezer takes the stage at #iHeartFestival! 💙🎸

More show details: https://t.co/4lzimzHcfk pic.twitter.com/MSttqYHxxf

— iHeartRadio (@iHeartRadio) June 2, 2026

From there, whip out the cowboy hats and put the spurs on the cowboy boots to scoot and boogie to the country music charm of Kenny Chesney. Rounding things off, plunge into the 'Lush Life' and dance under the 'Midnight Sun' with Zara Larsson's perfect pop princess energy as she rocks the stage and commands the spotlight.

Hold on to the high of night one as night two presents an equally epic lineup. Have yourself a delicious scoop of the sweetest "Moonbeam Ice Cream" as Benson Boone blows the crowd away with his amazing vocal prowess and captivating stage presence before handing things over to country music royalty Lainey Wilson. Keeping the momentum going, Major Lazer will definitely give you something to 'Lean On' with their solid mix of EDM and dancehall beats, turning the arena into a full-fledged dance floor.

No chill allowed. Only ENERGY. @MAJORLAZER is coming to Vegas! 🔊🔥🌴

Get all the #iHeartFestival info you need to come join us in September: https://t.co/4lzimzHK4S pic.twitter.com/Kmy5a80pyO

— iHeartRadio (@iHeartRadio) June 2, 2026

Don't miss the unmistakable pull of Muse's rock versatility, which shines through in hits like 'Supermassive Black Hole', 'Uprising', 'Hysteria', and so many more. Slowing things down with effortless swagger, bask in the heat of Snoop Dogg's laid-back hip-hop legacy as he takes the stage and lays down beats that have defined generations.

West Coast legend incoming - @SnoopDogg is headed to the #iHeartFestival! 🐾😮‍💨🌴

Come party with us in Vegas this September: https://t.co/4lzimzHcfk pic.twitter.com/Cap3uUoFlT

— iHeartRadio (@iHeartRadio) June 2, 2026

With more artists yet to be announced, the lineup is already shaping up to be a combination of some of the greatest artists of our generation. Bringing together chart-topping superstars, genre-defining legends, and rising talents from across the musical spectrum, the festival promises two unforgettable nights packed with iconic performances and crowd-pleasing hits. Whether you're drawn to K-pop, rock, hip-hop, country, EDM, or pop, the iHeartRadio Music Festival 2026 is set to deliver a celebration of music that transcends genres and generations. Click here for more info on the lineup and ticketing updates.

items.body:
At a time when economics often dictates the size and scope of a jazz group, adding a guitarist to a typical piano-bass-drums trio makes a world of difference. And when said guitarist is Peter Bernstein, the difference is even more pronounced. That gives bassist Harvie S a clear headstart on Bright Dawn, a modest studio date with Bernstein broadening the usual trio setting on the bassist's 21st recording as leader of his own ensemble—the first, however, following a 15-year hiatus.

The other members of Harvie's group, each of whom plays a pivotal role, are pianist Miki Hayama (Fender Rhodes on "Ghosts of Havana" and "Voice in the Sky") and drummer Matt Wilson who introduces and sparks the perky "I've Got Rhythm and Blues." That is one of Harvie's eight compositions, escorting Bob Dorough's playful "Devil May Care" and Chick Corea's sunny "Humpty Dumpty."

And therein lies the session's most problematic aspect. Even though decent and well-intentioned, Harvie's compositions are, to be frank, several lengthy strides away from memorable. While that may be traced in part to the group's makeup and Harvie S's resolve to lead the way, the fact remains that the success of any collective enterprise, regardless of size or shape, rests in large measure on its choice of material, and most of the songs on Bright Dawn simply don't measure up, even with Bernstein on board to help enliven them.

Harvie must be given props for naming one of his themes "Navalny" (and enhancing it with arco and string bass) but even that melody seems tame when compared to what comes next, the spunky "Rhythm and Blues," one of the session's few high spots. Hayama is an impressive soloist, as is Bernstein, and their expertise must be noted. That is not, however, nearly enough to raise Bright Dawn above the norm.

Ghosts of Havana; Devil May Care; Waltz for Vartan; Navalny; I've Got Rhythm and Blues; Yukimi's Song; Humpty Dumpty; The Truth; Voice in the Sky; Swithering.
